title.raw: 卷57 高祐 崔挺 Volume 57: Gao You, Cui Ting

sentences.zh: 高祐 崔挺

translations.literal: Gao You; Cui Ting
translations.idiomatic: Gao You; Cui Ting

sentences.zh: 高祐，字子集，小名次奴，勃海人也。

translations.literal: Gao You, courtesy name Ziji, childhood name Cinu, was a man of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao You, whose courtesy name was Ziji and whose childhood name was Cinu, came from Bohai.

sentences.zh: 本名禧，以與咸陽王同名，高祖賜名祐。

translations.literal: His original name was Xi; because it was the same as the Prince of Xianyang's name, Emperor Gaozu bestowed upon him the name You.
translations.idiomatic: His birth name had been Xi, but because it matched that of the Prince of Xianyang, Emperor Gaozu gave him the name You.

sentences.zh: 司空允從祖弟也。

translations.literal: He was a younger cousin of the Commandant of Works Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He was a younger cousin of Gao Yun, the Commandant of Works.

sentences.zh: 祖展，慕容寶黃門郎，太祖平中山，內徙京師，卒於三都大官。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhan was an Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gates under Murong Bao; when Emperor Taizu pacified Zhongshan, he was moved inland to the capital and died as Director of the Three Capitals' Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhan had served Murong Bao as Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gates; after Emperor Taizu conquered Zhongshan, the family was relocated to the capital, and Zhan died in office as Director of the Three Capitals' Granaries.

sentences.zh: 父讜，從世祖滅赫連昌，以功拜游擊將軍，賜爵南皮子。

translations.literal: His father Dan followed Emperor Shizu in destroying Helian Chang and, for merit, was appointed General of Mobile Cavalry and enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanpi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dan had followed Emperor Shizu in the campaign that destroyed Helian Chang; for his service he was made General of Mobile Cavalry and granted the title Marquis of Nanpi.

sentences.zh: 與崔浩共參著作，遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Together with Cui Hao he took part in compiling the histories and was promoted to Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He worked with Cui Hao on the historical compilations and was promoted to Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 轉給事中、冀青二州中正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and Rectifier for Ji and Qing provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and Rectifier for the two provinces of Ji and Qing.

sentences.zh: 假散騎常侍、平東將軍、蓨縣侯，使高麗。

translations.literal: He was provisionally made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the East, and Marquis of Tiao County, and sent as envoy to Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: He received provisional appointment as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and General Who Pacifies the East, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Tiao County, and was dispatched on a mission to Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈安南將軍、冀州刺史、假滄水公，諡曰康。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously given General Who Pacifies the South, Governor of Ji Province, and provisional title Duke of Cangshui; his posthumous name was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Ji Province, with the provisional title Duke of Cangshui; his posthumous name was Kang.

sentences.zh: 祐兄祚，襲爵，東青州刺史。

translations.literal: You's elder brother Zuo inherited the title and became Governor of Eastern Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: You's elder brother Zuo inherited the family title and served as Governor of Eastern Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 祐博涉書史，好文字雜說，材性通放，不拘小節。

translations.literal: You was broadly versed in books and histories, loved philology and miscellaneous learning, and by nature was open and free, not bound by petty rules.
translations.idiomatic: You had wide learning in books and histories, delighted in philology and assorted lore, and was by nature open and unconventional, caring little for petty proprieties.

sentences.zh: 初拜中書學生，轉博士、侍郎。

translations.literal: He was first appointed a student of the Central Secretariat, then transferred to Erudite and Gentleman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service as a student of the Central Secretariat, then rose to Erudite and Gentleman Attendant.

sentences.zh: 以祐招下邵郡羣賊之功，賜爵建康子。

translations.literal: For You's merit in winning over the bandits of Shao Commandery, he was granted the title Viscount of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Because You had persuaded the bandit groups of Shao Commandery to submit, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 高宗末，兗州東郡吏獲一異獸，獻之京師，時人咸無識者。

translations.literal: Near the end of Emperor Gaozong's reign, an official of Dong Commandery in Yan Province captured a strange beast and presented it in the capital, but no one of the time could identify it.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the reign of Emperor Gaozong, an official of Dong Commandery in Yan Province caught a strange animal and sent it to the capital, yet no one at court could name it.

sentences.zh: 詔以問祐，祐曰：「此是三吳所出，厥名鯪鯉，餘域率無，今我獲之，吳楚之地，其有歸國者乎？」

translations.literal: An edict ordered that You be asked; You said: "This creature comes from the Three Wu regions; its name is the lingli fish, and other lands generally do not have it. Now that we have obtained it, might there be those in the lands of Wu and Chu who will return to our state?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered You consulted. You replied, "This animal comes from the Three Wu regions; it is called the lingli, and other domains scarcely produce it. Now that we have captured one, does this not mean that the lands of Wu and Chu may yield up those who will return to our rule?"

sentences.zh: 又有人於零丘得玉印一以獻，詔以示祐，祐曰：「印上有籀書二字，文曰『宋壽』。

translations.literal: Again someone obtained a jade seal at Lingqiu and presented it; an edict showed it to You, and You said: "On the seal are two characters in seal script, reading 'Song Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward someone found a jade seal at Lingqiu and presented it to the throne. When the edict directed that it be shown to You, he said, "The seal bears two characters in seal script, reading 'Song Shou.

sentences.zh: 壽者，命也，我獲其命，亦是歸我之徵。」

translations.literal: Shou' means life or mandate; we have obtained their mandate—this too is a sign that they will return to us."
translations.idiomatic: Shou means life or mandate. That we have seized their mandate is likewise a sign that they will submit to us."

sentences.zh: 顯祖初，劉義隆子義陽王昶來奔，薛安都等以五州降附，時謂祐言有驗。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xianzu's reign, Liu Yilong's son, the Prince of Yiyang Liu Chang, came over in flight, and Xue Andu and others surrendered five provinces; people of the time said You's words had been verified.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Emperor Xianzu, Liu Chang, Prince of Yiyang and son of Liu Yilong of Song, defected to Wei, and Xue Andu and others surrendered five provinces. Contemporary opinion held that You's prophecies had been fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 高祖拜祕書令。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu appointed him Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu appointed him Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後與丞李彪等奏曰：「臣等聞典謨興，話言所以光著；

translations.literal: Later, together with Vice Director Li Biao and others, he memorialized: "Your subjects have heard that when the canons and counsels arose, spoken words were thereby made illustrious;
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Vice Director Li Biao and others in a memorial that read, "We have heard that when the canons and counsels were established, spoken words were thereby brought to light;

sentences.zh: 載籍作，成事所以昭揚。

translations.literal: when written records were made, accomplished deeds were thereby proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: and when written records were compiled, accomplished deeds were thereby made known.

sentences.zh: 然則尚書者記言之體，春秋者錄事之辭。

translations.literal: Thus the Documents records the form of words spoken, and the Spring and Autumn Annals records the language of events.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Documents preserves the form of recorded speech, and the Spring and Autumn Annals preserves the language of recorded events.

sentences.zh: 尋覽前志，斯皆言動之實錄也。

translations.literal: Searching through earlier chronicles, these are all true records of words and deeds.
translations.idiomatic: When one surveys the chronicles of earlier ages, all are faithful records of words and actions.

sentences.zh: 夏殷以前，其文弗具。

translations.literal: Before the Xia and Yin dynasties, the texts are not complete.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Xia and Shang, the written records are incomplete.

sentences.zh: 自周以降，典章備舉。

translations.literal: From the Zhou downward, statutes and regulations were fully set forth.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhou dynasty onward, statutes and regulations were fully established.

sentences.zh: 史官之體，文質不同；

translations.literal: The form of the historiographer's office differed in literary ornament and plainness;
translations.idiomatic: The institutions of the historiographer's office varied in literary style and plainness;

sentences.zh: 立書之旨，隨時有異。

translations.literal: the aim in establishing books changed with the times.
translations.idiomatic: and the purpose of compiling books shifted with each age.

sentences.zh: 至若左氏，屬詞比事，兩致並書，可謂存史意，而非全史體。

translations.literal: As for Master Zuo, he grouped words and compared events, writing both aspects together; this may be called preserving the historian's intent, but it is not the complete form of history.
translations.idiomatic: Master Zuo grouped words and compared events, setting down both aspects together; this may be said to preserve the historian's intent, yet it is not the full structure of historical writing.

sentences.zh: 逮司馬遷、班固，皆博識大才，論敍今古，曲有條章，雖周達未兼，斯實前史之可言者也。

translations.literal: When it came to Sima Qian and Ban Gu, both were men of vast learning and great talent; in narrating past and present they had subtle organization, and although comprehensive mastery was not combined in one, these are truly the earlier histories that may be spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of Sima Qian and Ban Gu, both were men of vast learning and great talent; in narrating past and present they achieved subtle organization. Though neither combined every virtue in full measure, these are truly the earlier histories worth speaking of.

sentences.zh: 至於後漢、魏、晉咸以放焉。

translations.literal: As for the Later Han, Wei, and Jin, all were lax in this regard.
translations.idiomatic: The histories of Later Han, Wei, and Jin, by contrast, all fell short.

sentences.zh: 惟聖朝創制上古，開基長發，自始均以後，至於成帝，其間世數久遠，是以史弗能傳。

translations.literal: Only our sage dynasty created institutions from high antiquity and opened a foundation of long flourishing; from Shizu onward to Emperor Cheng, the generations in between are remote in time, and therefore history could not be transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Our sage dynasty alone created institutions reaching back to high antiquity and laid a foundation meant to flourish for ages; yet from the era of Shizu down to Emperor Cheng the span of generations is so remote that history could not be fully transmitted.

sentences.zh: 臣等疏陋，忝當史職，披覽國記，竊有志焉。

translations.literal: Your subjects are shallow and crude, yet we undeservedly hold the office of historiographer; in perusing the dynastic records, we privately harbor this ambition.
translations.idiomatic: We are unworthy and shallow men who yet hold the office of historiographer; in reading the dynastic records, we have privately cherished this ambition.

sentences.zh: 愚謂自王業始基，庶事草創，皇始以降，光宅中土，宜依遷固大體，令事類相從，紀傳區別，表志殊貫，如此修綴，事可備盡。

translations.literal: We foolishly hold that from the beginning of royal enterprise and the founding of myriad affairs in their first draft, and from Huangshi onward when the realm was illuminated in the central land, one should follow the great structure of Qian and Gu, letting categories of events follow one another, distinguishing annals and biographies, and separating tables and treatises—if compiled thus, matters can be made complete.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly propose that from the founding of the royal enterprise and the first drafting of affairs, and from Huangshi onward when the dynasty took luminous possession of the central realm, the court should follow the grand model of Sima Qian and Ban Gu: let events be grouped by kind, distinguish annals from biographies, and set tables and treatises in their proper places. Compiled in this way, the record can be made complete.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下先天開物，洪宣帝命，太皇太后淳曜二儀，惠和王度，聲教之所漸洽，風譯之所覃加，固已義振前王矣。

translations.literal: We bow before Your Majesty, who before Heaven opened the creation and broadly proclaimed the imperial mandate; the Grand Empress Dowager purified the radiance of the Two Principles and harmonized the royal measure; where sound instruction has gradually pervaded and transforming influence has broadly extended, righteousness has already stirred the former kings.
translations.idiomatic: We bow before Your Majesty, who before Heaven opened the creation and broadly proclaimed the imperial mandate; the Grand Empress Dowager has purified the radiance of the Two Principles and harmonized the royal measure. Wherever sound instruction has gradually spread and transforming influence has broadly extended, righteousness has already surpassed that of the kings of old.

sentences.zh: 加太和以降，年未一紀，然嘉符禎瑞，備臻於往時；

translations.literal: Moreover, from the Taihe era onward, not yet one full cycle of years has passed, yet auspicious tokens and blessed omens have all arrived as in former times;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since the Taihe era began, less than twelve years have passed, yet auspicious signs and blessed omens have already matched those of former ages;

sentences.zh: 洪功茂德，事萃於曩世。

translations.literal: great achievements and abundant virtue gather together as in ages past.
translations.idiomatic: and great achievements and abundant virtue have gathered as in ages past.

sentences.zh: 會稽佇玉牒之章，岱宗想石記之列。

translations.literal: At Kuaiji they await the chapter of the jade register; at Mount Dai they long for the array of stone inscriptions.
translations.idiomatic: At Kuaiji men await the chapter of the jade register; at Mount Tai they long for the array of stone inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 而祕府策勳，述美未盡。

translations.literal: Yet in the secret archives the recording of merit and the narration of excellence are not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the secret archives the recording of merit and the narration of excellence remain unfinished.

sentences.zh: 將令皇風大猷，或闕而不載；

translations.literal: This would cause the great imperial wind and great design to be wanting and not recorded;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the great imperial ethos and grand design may be left out and unrecorded;

sentences.zh: 功臣懿績，或遺而弗傳。

translations.literal: meritorious ministers and excellent achievements may be left behind and not transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: and the deeds of meritorious ministers and outstanding achievements may be lost and never transmitted.

sentences.zh: 著作郎已下，請取有才用者，參造國書，如得其人，三年有成矣。

translations.literal: From the Gentleman for Compilation downward, we ask that men of talent and ability be selected to take part in composing the dynastic history; if the right men are obtained, in three years it can be completed.
translations.idiomatic: From the rank of Gentleman for Compilation downward, we ask that men of talent be chosen to help compose the dynastic history; with the right men, it can be finished in three years.

sentences.zh: 然後大明之德功，光于帝篇；

translations.literal: Then the virtue and achievement of great illumination will shine in the imperial annals;
translations.idiomatic: Then the virtue and achievements of great illumination will shine in the imperial annals;

sentences.zh: 聖后之勳業，顯于皇策。

translations.literal: the sage empress's meritorious work will appear in the imperial records.
translations.idiomatic: and the sage empress's meritorious work will appear in the imperial records.

sentences.zh: 佐命忠貞之倫，納言司直之士，咸以備著載籍矣。」

translations.literal: The company of those who aided the mandate with loyalty, and the men who remonstrated and kept straight accounts, will all be fully set forth in the written records."
translations.idiomatic: Those who aided the mandate with loyal service, and the remonstrating officials who kept the court straight, will all be fully set forth in the written records."

sentences.zh: 高祖從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu followed their advice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 高祖從容問祐曰：「比水旱不調，五穀不熟，何以止災而致豐稔？」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, at his ease, asked You: "Recently floods and droughts have been out of harmony and the five grains have not ripened—how may disasters be stopped and abundance brought about?"
translations.idiomatic: At leisure Emperor Gaozu asked You, "Lately floods and droughts have fallen out of harmony and the five grains have failed to ripen. How can disasters be halted and abundance secured?"

sentences.zh: 祐對曰：「昔堯湯之運，不能去陽九之會，陛下道同前聖，其如小旱何？

translations.literal: You replied: "In former times the fortunes of Yao and Tang could not escape the meeting of the yang-nine calamities; Your Majesty's Way matches the former sages—what is a small drought to that?
translations.idiomatic: You replied, "Even in the ages of Yao and Tang the cycle of yang-nine calamities could not be avoided. Your Majesty's Way equals that of the former sages—what is a minor drought beside that?

sentences.zh: 但當旌賢佐政，敬授民時，則災消穰至矣。」

translations.literal: Only honor the worthy and assist in government, respectfully grant the seasons to the people, and disasters will vanish and abundance will arrive."
translations.idiomatic: Only honor the worthy and assist in government, and respectfully grant the seasons to the people—then disasters will fade and abundance will come."

sentences.zh: 又問止盜之方，祐曰：「昔宋均樹德，[1]害獸不過其鄉；

translations.literal: He also asked the method for stopping banditry. You said: "In former times Song Jun planted virtue, [1] and harmful beasts did not pass his district;
translations.idiomatic: He also asked how to stop banditry. You said, "In former times Song Jun cultivated virtue, [1] and harmful beasts would not cross his district;

sentences.zh: 卓茂善教，蝗蟲不入其境。

translations.literal: Zhuo Mao was skilled in instruction, and locusts did not enter his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo Mao excelled in instruction, and locusts did not enter his territory.

sentences.zh: 彼盜賊者，人也，苟訓之有方，寧不易息。

translations.literal: Those bandits and thieves are human beings; if they are instructed by proper methods, would they not easily cease?
translations.idiomatic: Bandits and thieves are human beings; if they are instructed by proper methods, will they not easily cease?

sentences.zh: 當須宰守貞良，則盜止矣。」

translations.literal: What is needed are magistrates and guardians who are upright and good—then banditry will stop."
translations.idiomatic: What is needed are upright and capable magistrates and guardians—then banditry will cease."

sentences.zh: 祐又上疏云：「今之選舉，不採識治之優劣，專簡年勞之多少，斯非盡才之謂。

translations.literal: You also submitted a memorial saying: "In present selections for office, they do not examine the superiority or inferiority of knowledge and governance, but specialize in measuring years of service—this is not what is meant by employing all talent.
translations.idiomatic: You also submitted a memorial stating, "Present selections for office do not weigh a candidate's grasp of governance, but look only at years of service. This is not what is meant by employing all available talent.

sentences.zh: 宜停此薄藝，棄彼朽勞，唯才是舉，則官方斯穆。

translations.literal: It is fitting to stop this slight regard for minor arts, discard that rotten regard for seniority, and promote only by talent—then the official ranks will be harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: The court should cease rewarding petty accomplishments, discard worn-out seniority, and promote men solely for talent—then the official ranks will be put in good order.

sentences.zh: 又勳舊之臣，雖年勤可錄，而才非撫人者，則可加之以爵賞，不宜委之以方任，所謂王者可私人以財，不私人以官者也。」

translations.literal: Again, for meritorious old ministers, although years of diligence may be recorded, if their talent is not suited to governing people, then titles and rewards may be added to them, but regional responsibilities should not be entrusted to them—this is what is meant by saying that a king may give a man his private wealth, but not his private office."
translations.idiomatic: Again, for meritorious old ministers, though long service may be recorded, if their talent is not suited to governing people, they may be given titles and rewards, but they should not be entrusted with regional command. As the saying goes, a king may give a man his private wealth, but not his private office."

sentences.zh: 高祖皆善之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu approved all of this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu approved all of these proposals.

sentences.zh: 加給事中、冀州大中正，餘如故。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and Senior Rectifier of Ji Province; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and Senior Rectifier of Ji Province; his other offices remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 時李彪專統著作，祐為令，時相關豫而已。

translations.literal: At the time Li Biao alone directed the compilation, while You was Director; they merely consulted with one another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Biao alone directed the historical compilation, while You held the directorship; the two merely consulted with each other as needed.

sentences.zh: 出為持節、輔國將軍、西兗州刺史，假東光侯，鎮滑臺。

translations.literal: He went out as Bearer of the Staff, General Who Assists the State, and Governor of Western Yan Province, provisionally Marquis of Dongguang, stationed at Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Bearer of the Staff, General Who Assists the State, and Governor of Western Yan Province, with the provisional title Marquis of Dongguang, and was stationed at Huatai.

sentences.zh: 祐以郡國雖有太學，縣黨宜有黌序，乃縣立講學，黨立小學。

translations.literal: You held that although commanderies and principalities had the Imperial University, districts and townships ought to have schools, and so he established lecture halls in districts and elementary schools in townships.
translations.idiomatic: You held that although commanderies and principalities had the Imperial University, districts and townships still needed schools, and so he established lecture halls at the district level and elementary schools at the township level.

sentences.zh: [2]又令一家之中，自立一碓，五家之外，共造一井，以供行客，不聽婦人寄舂取水。

translations.literal: [2] He also ordered that within one household a single mortar-pestle be set up independently, and beyond five households they jointly build one well to supply traveling guests, not permitting women to pound grain or draw water on others' behalf.
translations.idiomatic: [2] He also ordered each household to maintain its own mortar, while groups of five households or more were to dig a shared well for travelers' use, and forbade women from pounding grain or drawing water on others' behalf.

sentences.zh: 又設禁賊之方，令五五相保，若盜發則連其坐，初雖似煩碎，後風化大行，寇盜止息。

translations.literal: He also set up methods for prohibiting bandits, ordering groups of five to guarantee one another; if theft occurred, the whole group was implicated. At first this seemed troublesome in detail, but afterward custom and instruction spread widely and raiders and thieves ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He also instituted measures against banditry, requiring groups of five households to guarantee one another; if theft broke out, the whole group was held liable. At first the rules seemed burdensome, but in time custom and instruction took hold, and raiders and thieves disappeared.

sentences.zh: 子和璧，字僧壽，有學問。

translations.literal: His son Hebi, courtesy name Sengshou, had learning.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hebi, whose courtesy name was Sengshou, was a learned man.

sentences.zh: 中書博士。

translations.literal: Erudite of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Erudite of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 和璧子顥，字門賢，學涉有時譽。

translations.literal: Hebi's son Hao, courtesy name Menxian, was learned and broadly accomplished and enjoyed reputation in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Hebi's son Hao, whose courtesy name was Menxian, was learned and accomplished and enjoyed a fine reputation in his day.

sentences.zh: 自司空參軍轉員外郎，襲爵建康子，遷符璽郎中。

translations.literal: From aide to the Commandant of Works he was transferred to Vice Director; he inherited the title Viscount of Jiankang and was promoted to Gentleman of the Seals and Credentials.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from aide to the Commandant of Works to Vice Director, inherited the title Viscount of Jiankang, and was promoted to Gentleman of the Seals and Credentials.

sentences.zh: 出為冀州別駕，未之任，屬刺史元愉據州反，世宗遣尚書李平為都督，率眾討之。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief Administrator of Ji Province but had not yet taken up the post when the governor Yuan Yu seized the province in rebellion; Emperor Shizong sent the Minister Li Ping as commander-in-chief to lead troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Chief Administrator of Ji Province but had not yet assumed the post when Governor Yuan Yu seized the province in rebellion. Emperor Shizong sent Minister Li Ping as commander-in-chief to lead troops against him.

sentences.zh: 平以顥彼州領袖，乃引為錄事參軍，仍領統軍，軍機取捨，多與參決。

translations.literal: Ping, because Hao was a leading figure of that province, brought him in as Recording Secretary and also put him in command of the army; in military decisions of what to adopt or discard, Hao took part in many deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hao was a leading figure in that province, Ping brought him in as Recording Secretary and also placed him in command of troops; on many military decisions Hao took part in the deliberations.

sentences.zh: 擒愉之後，別黨千餘人皆將伏法，顥以為擁逼之徒，前許原免，宜為表陳請。

translations.literal: After Yu was captured, more than a thousand of the separate faction were all to be executed by law; Hao held that these were men who had been coerced, and that since they had previously been promised pardon, a memorial should be submitted requesting it.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu was captured, more than a thousand members of the rebel faction were to be executed. Hao argued that these men had been coerced and that, since they had already been promised pardon, a memorial should be submitted on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 平從之，於是咸蒙全濟。

translations.literal: Ping followed this, and thereby all were fully spared.
translations.idiomatic: Ping agreed, and all were spared.

sentences.zh: 事定，顥仍述職。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Hao resumed his duties.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, Hao resumed his duties.

sentences.zh: 時軍旅之後，因之飢饉，顥為綱紀，務存寬靜，甚收時譽。

translations.literal: At the time, after the military campaign, famine followed in consequence; Hao set the regulations, striving to preserve leniency and calm, and greatly won the praise of the age.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign famine followed, and Hao set policy with an emphasis on leniency and calm, winning wide praise.

sentences.zh: 尋加陵江將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made General Who Crosses the River.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon additionally appointed General Who Crosses the River.

sentences.zh: 坐事免。

translations.literal: Because of an offense he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed because of an offense.

sentences.zh: 久之，除鎮遠將軍，遷輔國將軍、中散大夫，轉征虜將軍，仍中散。

translations.literal: After a long time he was made General Who Pacifies the Distant, then transferred to General Who Assists the State and Palace Attendant, then transferred to General Who Punishes the Barbarians while still serving as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant, then promoted to General Who Assists the State and Palace Attendant, then transferred to General Who Punishes the Barbarians while retaining his post as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒，時年四十九。

translations.literal: He died at the age of forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈平東將軍、滄州刺史，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Cang Province; his posthumous name was Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Cang Province; his posthumous name was Hui.

sentences.zh: 子德正，襲。

translations.literal: His son Dezheng inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dezheng inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 武定中，黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era he was Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wuding era he served as Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 顥弟雅，字興賢，有風度。

translations.literal: Hao's younger brother Ya, courtesy name Xingxian, had bearing and manner.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's younger brother Ya, whose courtesy name was Xingxian, had distinguished bearing.

sentences.zh: 自給事中稍遷司徒府錄事參軍、定州撫軍府長史。

translations.literal: From Attendant Within the Yellow Gates he was gradually promoted to Recording Secretary of the Minister of Education's office and Chief Clerk of the Pacification Army headquarters of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Attendant Within the Yellow Gates to Recording Secretary in the Ministry of Education and Chief Clerk of the Pacification Army headquarters in Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 卒，年三十四。

translations.literal: He died at the age of thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of thirty-four.

sentences.zh: 天平中，追贈散騎常侍、平北將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era he was posthumously given Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the North, and Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianping era he was posthumously honored as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the North, and Governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 子德乾，早有令問。

translations.literal: His son Degan had early a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His son Degan enjoyed a fine reputation from an early age.

sentences.zh: 任城太守。

translations.literal: Administrator of Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 雅弟諒，字脩賢。

translations.literal: Ya's younger brother Liang, courtesy name Xiuxian.
translations.idiomatic: Ya's younger brother Liang, whose courtesy name was Xiuxian.

sentences.zh: 少好學，多識強記，居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning, had broad knowledge and strong memory, and was known for filial piety in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning, had broad knowledge and a powerful memory, and was known for filial conduct during mourning.

sentences.zh: 太和末，京兆王愉開府辟召，高祖妙簡行佐，諒與隴西李仲尚、趙郡李鳳起等同時應選。

translations.literal: At the end of the Taihe era, the Prince of Jingzhao Yu opened a headquarters and summoned men; Emperor Gaozu finely selected traveling aides, and Liang, together with Li Zhongshang of Longxi, Li Fengqi of Zhao Commandery, and others, were chosen at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Taihe era, when the Prince of Jingzhao Yu opened his headquarters and summoned staff, Emperor Gaozu carefully selected traveling aides; Liang was chosen together with Li Zhongshang of Longxi, Li Fengqi of Zhao Commandery, and others.

sentences.zh: 稍遷太尉主簿、國子博士。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Chief Clerk of the Grand Marshal and Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Chief Clerk of the Grand Marshal and Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 正光中，加驍騎將軍，為徐州行臺。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era he was additionally made General of Valiant Cavalry and made Mobile Headquarters of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengguang era he was additionally appointed General of Valiant Cavalry and assigned to the mobile headquarters of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 至彭城，屬元法僧反叛，逼諒同之，諒不許，為法僧所害，時年四十一。

translations.literal: When he reached Pengcheng, Yuan Faseng rebelled and forced Liang to join him; Liang would not agree and was killed by Faseng at the age of forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Pengcheng, Yuan Faseng rebelled and tried to force Liang to join him. Liang refused and was killed by Faseng. He was forty-one.

sentences.zh: 朝廷痛惜之，贈左將軍、滄州刺史。

translations.literal: The court grieved for him and posthumously gave him General of the Left and Governor of Cang Province.
translations.idiomatic: The court mourned him and posthumously honored him as General of the Left and Governor of Cang Province.

sentences.zh: 又下詔，以諒臨危授命，誠節可重，復贈使持節、平北將軍、幽州刺史，贈帛二百匹，優一子出身，諡曰忠侯。

translations.literal: Another edict was issued, because Liang at the crisis entrusted his life, his loyal integrity being weighty; he was again posthumously given Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, and Governor of You Province, with two hundred bolts of silk, preferential entry into office for one son, and posthumous title Loyal Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: The court also issued an edict stating that because Liang had given his life at the crisis, his loyal integrity deserved honor. He was further posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, and Governor of You Province, together with two hundred bolts of silk, preferential entry into office for one son, and the posthumous title Loyal Marquis.

sentences.zh: 三子。

translations.literal: He had three sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons.

sentences.zh: 長惠勝，武定中，司徒外兵參軍。

translations.literal: The eldest was Huisheng; in the Wuding era he was Outer Aide of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son was Huisheng, who during the Wuding era served as Outer Aide of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 諒造親表譜錄四十許卷，自五世已下，內外曲盡。

translations.literal: Liang compiled a genealogical record of kin and clan tables in some forty scrolls, from the fifth generation downward, fully treating inner and outer branches.
translations.idiomatic: Liang compiled a genealogical record of kin and clan tables in some forty scrolls, covering from the fifth generation downward and treating both inner and outer branches in full detail.

sentences.zh: 覽者服其博記。

translations.literal: Readers admired his broad record-keeping.
translations.idiomatic: Readers marveled at the breadth of his record-keeping.

sentences.zh: 祐弟欽，幼隨從叔濟使於劉義隆，還為中書學生，遷祕書中散。

translations.literal: You's younger brother Qin, in youth followed his father's younger cousin Ji on a mission to Liu Yilong; on returning he became a student of the Central Secretariat and was promoted to Palace Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: You's younger brother Qin had in youth accompanied his father's younger cousin Ji on a mission to Liu Yilong of Song; on his return he became a student of the Central Secretariat and was promoted to Palace Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 年四十餘，卒。

translations.literal: At over forty years of age he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his forties.

sentences.zh: 子法永，諸王從事中郎。

translations.literal: His son Fayong was Attendant of the Princes.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fayong served as Attendant of the Princes.

sentences.zh: 亦早亡。

translations.literal: He too died young.
translations.idiomatic: He too died young.

sentences.zh: 祐從父弟次同，永安末，撫軍將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: You's younger cousin Citong, at the end of the Yong'an era, was General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: You's younger cousin Citong, late in the Yong'an era, served as General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 子乾邕，永熙中，司空公、長樂郡開國公。

translations.literal: His son Qianyong, in the Yongxi era, was Duke of the Commandant of Works and Duke Who Founded the State of Changle Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qianyong, during the Yongxi era, held the titles Duke of the Commandant of Works and Duke Who Founded the State of Changle Commandery.

sentences.zh: 乾邕弟敖曹，天平中，司徒公、京兆郡開國公。

translations.literal: Qianyong's younger brother Aocao, in the Tianping era, was Duke of the Minister of Education and Duke Who Founded the State of Jingzhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyong's younger brother Aocao, during the Tianping era, held the titles Duke of the Minister of Education and Duke Who Founded the State of Jingzhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 崔挺，字雙根，博陵安平人也。

translations.literal: Cui Ting, courtesy name Shuanggen, was a man of Anping in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ting, whose courtesy name was Shuanggen, came from Anping in Boling.

sentences.zh: 六世祖贊，魏尚書僕射。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Zan was Vice Director of the Masters of Writing in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Zan had served as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing in Wei.

sentences.zh: 五世祖洪，晉吏部尚書。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Hong was Director of the Ministry of Personnel in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Hong had been Director of the Ministry of Personnel under Jin.

sentences.zh: 父鬱，濮陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Yu was Administrator of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu had served as Administrator of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 挺幼居喪盡禮。

translations.literal: Ting in youth observed mourning to the full in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Ting observed mourning with full propriety.

sentences.zh: 少敦學業，多所覽究，推人愛士，州閭親附焉。

translations.literal: In youth he was earnest in studies, broadly read and investigated, promoted others and loved scholars, and the district and neighborhood drew close to him.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he applied himself to learning, read widely, promoted others and cherished scholars, and won the affection of his district and neighbors.

sentences.zh: 每四時與鄉人父老書相存慰，辭旨款備，得者榮之。

translations.literal: Each season he exchanged letters of inquiry and consolation with the elders of his township; the wording was warm and complete, and those who received them took it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Each season he exchanged letters of inquiry and consolation with the elders of his township; his wording was warm and complete, and those who received them counted it an honor.

sentences.zh: 三世同居，門有禮讓。

translations.literal: Three generations lived together, and the household was marked by courtesy and yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations lived under one roof, and the household was known for courtesy and mutual deference.

sentences.zh: 於後頻值飢年，家始分析，挺與弟振推讓田宅舊資，惟守墓田而已。

translations.literal: Afterward they frequently encountered famine years, and the family then divided; Ting and his younger brother Zhen yielded fields, houses, and old assets to one another, keeping only the grave-plot fields.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after repeated years of famine, the family divided its property; Ting and his younger brother Zhen yielded fields, houses, and old assets to one another, keeping only the grave-plot fields.

sentences.zh: 家徒壁立，兄弟怡然，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: The household was bare as walls standing alone, yet the brothers were at ease, never letting books leave their hands.
translations.idiomatic: The household was reduced to bare walls, yet the brothers remained content and never let their books leave their hands.

sentences.zh: 時穀糴踊貴，鄉人或有贍者，遺挺，辭讓而受，仍亦散之貧困，不為畜積，故鄉邑更欽歎焉。

translations.literal: At the time grain prices soared; some township people who could support others sent gifts to Ting; he declined but then accepted, and still distributed them to the poor, making no store of wealth, and so the district admired him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When grain prices soared, some townspeople who could spare food sent gifts to Ting. He declined at first but then accepted, and immediately distributed them to the poor without hoarding anything, which won still greater admiration in his district.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，射策高第，拜中書博士，轉中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was recommended as a cultivated talent, achieved a high rank in the archery-and-policy examination, was appointed Erudite of the Central Secretariat, and was transferred to Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as a cultivated talent, he ranked high in the policy examination, was appointed Erudite of the Central Secretariat, and was promoted to Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以工書，受敕於長安書文明太后父燕宣王碑，賜爵泰昌子。

translations.literal: Because of skill in calligraphy, he received an edict to write at Chang'an the stele of the Empress Dowager Wenming's father, the Prince of Yan and King of Xuan, and was granted the title Viscount of Taichang.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his skill in calligraphy, he received an edict to inscribe at Chang'an the stele of the Empress Dowager Wenming's father, the Prince of Yan and King of Xuan, and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Taichang.

sentences.zh: 轉登聞令，遷典屬國下大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Gate of Hearing Petitions and promoted to Grand Master of the Dependent States.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of the Gate of Hearing Petitions and promoted to Grand Master of the Dependent States.

sentences.zh: 以參議律令，賜布帛八百匹、穀八百石、馬牛各二。

translations.literal: For participating in deliberation on statutes and ordinances, he was given eight hundred bolts of cloth and silk, eight hundred piculs of grain, and two horses and two oxen.
translations.idiomatic: For participating in deliberation on statutes and ordinances, he was rewarded with eight hundred bolts of cloth and silk, eight hundred piculs of grain, and two horses and two oxen.

sentences.zh: 尚書李沖甚重之。

translations.literal: The Minister Li Chong greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Li Chong held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 高祖以挺女為嬪。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu took Ting's daughter as a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu took Ting's daughter into the palace as a concubine.

sentences.zh: 太和十八年，大將軍、宋王劉昶南鎮彭城，詔假立義將軍，為昶府長史，以疾辭免，乃以王肅為長史。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Taihe, the Grand General and Prince of Song Liu Chang was stationed in the south at Pengcheng; an edict provisionally made Ting General Who Establishes Righteousness and Chief Clerk of Chang's headquarters, but he declined because of illness and was replaced by Wang Su as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Taihe, when the Grand General and Prince of Song Liu Chang was stationed at Pengcheng in the south, an edict provisionally appointed Ting General Who Establishes Righteousness and Chief Clerk of Chang's headquarters. Ting declined because of illness, and Wang Su was appointed in his place.

sentences.zh: 其被寄遇如此。

translations.literal: Such was the trust and favor shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the degree of trust and favor he enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 後除昭武將軍、光州刺史，威恩並著，風化大行。

translations.literal: Later he was made General Who Displays Martiality and Governor of Guang Province; authority and kindness were both manifest, and transforming instruction spread widely.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed General Who Displays Martiality and Governor of Guang Province, where his authority and kindness were both manifest and transforming instruction spread widely.

sentences.zh: 十九年，車駕幸兗州，召挺赴行在所。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the imperial carriage visited Yan Province and summoned Ting to the traveling headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the emperor visited Yan Province and summoned Ting to the traveling headquarters.

sentences.zh: 及見，引諭優厚。

translations.literal: When he was received, he was drawn forward and instructed with exceptional kindness.
translations.idiomatic: When he was received, the emperor drew him forward and addressed him with exceptional kindness.

sentences.zh: 又問挺治邊之略，因及文章。

translations.literal: He also asked Ting about strategy for governing the frontier, and then spoke of literature.
translations.idiomatic: He also questioned Ting about strategy for governing the frontier and then spoke of literature.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚悅，謂挺曰：「別卿已來，倐焉二載，吾所綴文，已成一集，今當給卿副本，時可觀之。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased and said to Ting: "Since I parted from you, two years have swiftly passed. The pieces I have strung together have already become one collection, and I shall now give you a copy to read at your leisure."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased and said to Ting, "Since we parted, two years have swiftly passed. The pieces I have composed have already filled one collection, and I shall now give you a copy to read at your leisure."

sentences.zh: 又顧謂侍臣曰：「擁旄者悉皆如此，吾何憂哉。」

translations.literal: He then turned and said to the attending officials: "If all who bear command banners are like this, what have I to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: He then turned to the attending officials and said, "If all who bear command banners are like this, what have I to worry about?"

sentences.zh: 復還州。

translations.literal: He then returned to his province.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned to his province.

sentences.zh: 及散騎常侍張彝兼侍中巡行風俗，見挺政化之美，謂挺曰：「彝受使省方，採察謠訟，入境觀政，實愧清使之名。」

translations.literal: When Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Zhang Yi, also serving as Palace Attendant, toured to inspect local customs, he saw the beauty of Ting's governance and transformation and said to Ting: "Yi received a mission to inspect the regions, gather popular songs and lawsuits, and observe government on entering a territory—I am truly ashamed of the name 'clear envoy.'"
translations.idiomatic: When Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Zhang Yi, also serving as Palace Attendant, toured the provinces to inspect local customs, he saw the excellence of Ting's governance and said to him, "Yi was sent to inspect the regions, gather popular songs and lawsuits, and observe government on entering each territory—I am truly ashamed of the title 'clear envoy.'"

sentences.zh: 州治舊掖城，西北數里有斧山，峯嶺高峻，北臨滄海，南望岱嶽，一邦遊觀之地也。

translations.literal: The provincial seat was formerly at Ye City; several li to the northwest was Mount Fu, its peaks and ridges lofty and steep, facing the dark sea to the north and gazing toward Mount Dai to the south—a place for touring and viewing in the whole commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial seat was at Ye City; several li to the northwest stood Mount Fu, whose peaks rose steeply, facing the sea to the north and Mount Tai to the south—a favorite place of sightseeing in the whole commandery.

sentences.zh: 挺於頂上欲營觀宇，故老曰：「此嶺秋夏之際，常有暴雨迅風，巖石盡落，相傳云是龍道，恐此觀不可久立。」

translations.literal: Ting wished to build a viewing hall on the summit; the elders said: "On this ridge, between autumn and summer, there are often violent storms and swift winds, and the rocks all fall away. Tradition says this is the dragon's path, and I fear this hall cannot long stand."
translations.idiomatic: Ting wished to build a viewing hall on the summit. The elders said, "On this ridge, between autumn and summer, violent storms often strike and rocks tumble down. Tradition says this is the dragon's path, and I fear the hall cannot long stand."

sentences.zh: 挺曰：「人神相去，何遠之有？

translations.literal: Ting said: "How far apart are men and spirits, after all?
translations.idiomatic: Ting replied, "How far apart are men and spirits, after all?

sentences.zh: 虬龍倐忽，豈唯一路乎！」

translations.literal: A coiled dragon moves in a flash—surely it has more than one path!"
translations.idiomatic: A coiled dragon moves in a flash—surely it has more than one path!"

sentences.zh: 遂營之。

translations.literal: He then built it.
translations.idiomatic: He built it anyway.

sentences.zh: 數年間，果無風雨之異。

translations.literal: Within several years there were indeed no unusual storms.
translations.idiomatic: For several years there were indeed no unusual storms.

sentences.zh: 挺既代，即為風雹所毀，於後作，復尋壞，遂莫能立。

translations.literal: After Ting was replaced, it was destroyed by wind and hail; later builders restored it, but it was again soon ruined, and thereafter no one could keep it standing.
translations.idiomatic: After Ting left office, the hall was destroyed by wind and hail; later builders restored it, but it was soon ruined again, and thereafter no one could keep it standing.

sentences.zh: 眾以為善化所感。

translations.literal: The multitude held that this was a response to his good transforming influence.
translations.idiomatic: People believed this was a response to his virtuous transforming influence.

sentences.zh: 時以犯罪配邊者多有逃越，遂立重制，一人犯罪逋亡，合門充役。

translations.literal: At the time many who were sentenced for crimes to frontier assignment escaped, and so a severe regulation was established: if one person committed a crime and fled, the whole household was made to serve corvée.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many convicts assigned to the frontier escaped, and so a severe regulation was established: if one member of a household committed a crime and fled, the entire household was conscripted for corvée service.

sentences.zh: 挺上書，以為周書父子罪不相及。

translations.literal: Ting submitted a memorial, holding that in the Book of Zhou fathers' and sons' crimes do not extend to one another.
translations.idiomatic: Ting submitted a memorial arguing that in the Book of Zhou the crimes of fathers and sons do not extend to one another.

sentences.zh: 天下善人少，惡人多，以一人犯罪，延及合門。

translations.literal: Under Heaven good men are few and evil men many; because one person commits a crime, the whole household is implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Under Heaven good men are few and evil men many; to punish an entire household because one person has committed a crime is unjust.

sentences.zh: 司馬牛受桓魋之罰，柳下惠嬰盜跖之誅，豈不哀哉！

translations.literal: Sima Niu suffered punishment because of Huan Tui; the infant son of Liuxia Hui would have received the execution meted to Dao Zhi—how pitiful!
translations.idiomatic: Sima Niu suffered because of Huan Tui, and the infant son of Liuxia Hui would have shared the punishment of Dao Zhi—how pitiful!

sentences.zh: 辭甚雅切，高祖納之。

translations.literal: The wording was very elegant and earnest, and Emperor Gaozu adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The wording was elegant and earnest, and Emperor Gaozu accepted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 先是，州內少鐵，器用皆求之他境，挺表復鐵官，公私有賴。

translations.literal: Earlier, within the province iron was scarce and utensils all had to be sought from other regions; Ting memorialized to restore the iron office, and public and private affairs both depended on it.
translations.idiomatic: Previously iron was scarce in the province and utensils had to be obtained from other regions. Ting memorialized to restore the iron office, to the great benefit of both public and private affairs.

sentences.zh: 諸州中正，本在論人，高祖將辨天下氏族，仍亦訪定，乃遙授挺本州大中正。

translations.literal: The rectifiers of the various provinces were originally charged with evaluating men; Emperor Gaozu was about to distinguish clans throughout the realm and also sought to fix their rankings, and so he remotely appointed Ting Senior Rectifier of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: The rectifiers of the various provinces were originally charged with evaluating men. When Emperor Gaozu set out to classify clans throughout the realm and fix their rankings, he appointed Ting Senior Rectifier of his native province from afar.

sentences.zh: 掖縣有人，年踰九十，板輿造州。

translations.literal: In Ye County there was a man over ninety years old who came to the provincial seat in a carrying-chair.
translations.idiomatic: In Ye County there was a man over ninety who came to the provincial seat in a carrying-chair.

sentences.zh: 自稱少曾充使林邑，得一美玉，方尺四寸，甚有光彩，藏之海島，垂六十歲。

translations.literal: He said that in youth he had once served as envoy to Linyi and obtained a fine jade, one foot four inches square, very lustrous, which he hid on a sea island for nearly sixty years.
translations.idiomatic: He said that in youth he had served as envoy to Linyi and obtained a fine jade, one foot four inches square and very lustrous, which he had hidden on a sea island for nearly sixty years.

sentences.zh: 忻逢明治，今願奉之。

translations.literal: Rejoicing to meet enlightened governance, he now wished to present it.
translations.idiomatic: Rejoicing to meet enlightened governance, he now wished to present it as an offering.

sentences.zh: 挺曰：「吾雖德謝古人，未能以玉為寶。」

translations.literal: Ting said: "Although my virtue falls short of the ancients, I cannot take jade as a treasure."
translations.idiomatic: Ting said, "Although my virtue falls short of the ancients, I cannot treat jade as a treasure."

sentences.zh: 遣船隨取，光潤果然。

translations.literal: He sent a boat to fetch it, and its luster was indeed as described.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a boat to fetch it, and its luster was indeed as described.

sentences.zh: 竟不肯受，仍表送京都。

translations.literal: In the end he would not accept it, but instead memorialized to send it to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he would not accept it, but instead memorialized to send it to the capital.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，累表乞還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, he repeatedly memorialized asking to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, Ting repeatedly memorialized asking to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 景明初見代，老幼泣涕追隨，縑帛贈送，挺悉不納。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming he was replaced; old and young wept and followed him, presenting silk gifts, but Ting accepted none of them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingming era he was replaced; old and young wept and followed him, presenting gifts of silk, but Ting accepted none of them.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍趙脩得幸世宗，挺雖同州壤，未嘗詣門。

translations.literal: Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Zhao Xiu won favor with Emperor Shizong; although Ting was from the same province, he never called at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Zhao Xiu won favor with Emperor Shizong, but although Ting was from the same province, he never called at Zhao's gate.

sentences.zh: 北海王詳為司徒、錄尚書事，以挺為司馬，挺固辭不免。

translations.literal: The Prince of Beihai Xiang served as Minister of Education and recorded affairs of the Masters of Writing; he appointed Ting as Marshal, and though Ting firmly declined, he could not escape the post.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Beihai Xiang served as Minister of Education and recorded affairs of the Masters of Writing, he appointed Ting as Marshal. Ting firmly declined but could not escape the appointment.

sentences.zh: 世人皆歎其屈，而挺處之夷然。

translations.literal: People of the age all sighed that he was wronged, yet Ting bore it with calm ease.
translations.idiomatic: People of the age all lamented that he had been wronged, yet Ting bore it with calm ease.

sentences.zh: 於後詳攝選，眾人競稱考第，以求遷敍，挺終獨無言。

translations.literal: Later, when Xiang took charge of selections, everyone competed in proclaiming examination grades to seek promotion, but Ting alone remained silent to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Xiang took charge of selections, everyone competed in proclaiming examination grades to seek promotion, but Ting alone remained silent.

sentences.zh: 詳曰：「崔光州考級並未加授，宜投一牒，當為申請。

translations.literal: Xiang said: "Director Cui of Guang Province, your examination grade has not yet been conferred; you ought to submit a note, and I shall apply on your behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said, "Director Cui of Guang Province, your examination grade has not yet been conferred. You ought to submit a note, and I shall apply on your behalf.

sentences.zh: 蘧伯玉耻獨為君子，亦何故默然？」

translations.literal: Qu Boyu was ashamed to be the only gentleman—why then are you silent?"
translations.idiomatic: Qu Boyu was ashamed to be the only gentleman—why then are you silent?"

sentences.zh: 挺對曰：「階級是聖朝大例，考課亦國之恒典。

translations.literal: Ting replied: "Ranks and grades are the great precedent of the sage dynasty, and examinations are also the constant statute of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Ting replied, "Ranks and grades are the great precedent of the sage dynasty, and examinations are also the constant statute of the state.

sentences.zh: 下官雖慚古賢不伐之美，至於自衒求進，竊以羞之。」

translations.literal: Your subordinate, though ashamed before the ancients' virtue of not boasting, yet as for displaying himself to seek advancement, privately feels shame."
translations.idiomatic: Your subordinate, though he admires the ancients' virtue of not boasting, yet feels shame at displaying himself to seek advancement."

sentences.zh: 詳大相稱歎。

translations.literal: Xiang greatly praised and sighed over this.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang greatly praised and admired this.

sentences.zh: 自為司馬，詳未曾呼名，常稱州號，以示優禮。

translations.literal: From the time he became Marshal, Xiang never called him by personal name but always used his provincial title to show special courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Ting became Marshal, Xiang never called him by personal name but always used his provincial title to show special courtesy.

sentences.zh: 四年卒，時年五十九。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died at the age of fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，贈輔國將軍、幽州刺史，諡曰景。

translations.literal: That winter he was posthumously given General Who Assists the State and Governor of You Province; his posthumous name was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was posthumously honored as General Who Assists the State and Governor of You Province; his posthumous name was Jing.

sentences.zh: 光州故吏聞凶問，莫不悲感，共鑄八尺銅像於城東廣因寺，起八關齋，追奉冥福，其遺愛若此。

translations.literal: The former officials of Guang Province, on hearing the news of his death, were all grieved; together they cast an eight-foot bronze image at Guangyin Temple east of the city and established an eightfold fasting observance to seek blessings for him in the nether world—such was the lingering affection he left.
translations.idiomatic: The former officials of Guang Province, on hearing of his death, were all grief-stricken; together they cast an eight-foot bronze image at Guangyin Temple east of the city and established an eightfold fasting observance to seek blessings for him in the nether world—such was the affection he left behind.

sentences.zh: 初，崔光之在貧賤也，挺贍遺衣食，常親敬焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Cui Guang was in poverty and low station, Ting supplied him with food and clothing and always treated him with personal respect.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Cui Guang was poor and obscure, Ting supplied him with food and clothing and always treated him with personal respect.

sentences.zh: 又識邢巒、宋弁於童稚之中，並謂終當遠致。

translations.literal: He also recognized Xing Luan and Song Bian in their childhood and said of both that they would ultimately reach far.
translations.idiomatic: He also recognized Xing Luan and Song Bian in their childhood and predicted that both would rise to great eminence.

sentences.zh: 世稱其知人。

translations.literal: The age praised him for knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: His age praised him for knowing men.

sentences.zh: 歷官二十餘年，家資不益，食不重味，室無綺羅，閨門之內，雍雍如也。

translations.literal: Through more than twenty years in office his household wealth did not increase; he did not eat two flavors at one meal, his rooms had no brocade or gauze, and within the inner gates all was harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Through more than twenty years in office his household wealth did not increase; he ate no dish with more than one flavor, his rooms held no brocade or gauze, and within the inner gates all was harmonious.

sentences.zh: 舊故多有贈賵，諸子推挺素心，一無所受。

translations.literal: Old friends often sent funeral gifts; his sons, deferring to Ting's plain heart, accepted none of them.
translations.idiomatic: Old friends often sent funeral gifts, but his sons, deferring to Ting's plain-hearted ways, accepted none of them.

sentences.zh: 有子六人。

translations.literal: He had six sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons.

sentences.zh: 長子孝芬，字恭梓。

translations.literal: The eldest son was Xiaofen, courtesy name Gongzi.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son was Xiaofen, whose courtesy name was Gongzi.

sentences.zh: 早有才識，博學好文章。

translations.literal: He had early talent and insight, broad learning, and loved literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He showed talent and insight from an early age, had broad learning, and loved literary composition.

sentences.zh: 高祖召見，甚嗟賞之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu summoned him for an audience and greatly admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu summoned him for an audience and greatly admired him.

sentences.zh: 李彪謂挺曰：「比見賢子謁帝，旨諭殊優，今當為羣拜紀。」

translations.literal: Li Biao said to Ting: "Recently I saw your worthy son attend upon the emperor; his instructions were exceptionally favorable. He should now be recorded among those who bow in the assembly."
translations.idiomatic: Li Biao said to Ting, "Recently I saw your worthy son attend upon the emperor; his instructions were exceptionally favorable. He should now be recorded among those who bow in the assembly."

sentences.zh: 挺曰：「卿自欲善處人父子之間，然斯言吾所不敢聞也。」

translations.literal: Ting said: "You yourself wish to handle well the relations between father and son, but these words I dare not hear."
translations.idiomatic: Ting replied, "You yourself wish to handle well the relations between father and son, but these are words I dare not hear."

sentences.zh: 司徒、彭城王勰板為行參軍，後除著作郎，襲父爵。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education, the Prince of Pengcheng Xie, appointed him Traveling Aide; later he was made Gentleman for Compilation and inherited his father's title.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education, the Prince of Pengcheng Xie, appointed him Traveling Aide; later he was made Gentleman for Compilation and inherited his father's title.

sentences.zh: 尚書令高肇親寵權盛，子植除青州刺史，啟孝芬為司馬。

translations.literal: The Director of the Masters of Writing Gao Zhao was personally favored and his power flourished; his son Zhi was made Governor of Qing Province and recommended Xiaofen as Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Gao Zhao enjoyed personal favor and great power; his son Zhi was appointed Governor of Qing Province and recommended Xiaofen as Marshal.

sentences.zh: 後除司徒記室參軍、司空屬、定州大中正，長於剖判，甚有能名，府主任城王澄雅重之。

translations.literal: Later he was made Recording Secretary of the Minister of Education, Attendant of the Commandant of Works, and Senior Rectifier of Ding Province; he excelled in deciding cases and had a great reputation for ability; the Prince of Rencheng Cheng, head of the headquarters, greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Recording Secretary of the Minister of Education, Attendant of the Commandant of Works, and Senior Rectifier of Ding Province. He excelled in deciding cases and enjoyed a great reputation for ability; the Prince of Rencheng Cheng, head of the headquarters, greatly valued him.

sentences.zh: 熙平中，澄奏地制八條，孝芬所參定也。

translations.literal: In the Xiping era Cheng memorialized the eight articles on land regulation, which Xiaofen helped to fix.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiping era Cheng memorialized the eight articles on land regulation, which Xiaofen helped to draft.

sentences.zh: 在府久之，除龍驤將軍、廷尉少卿。

translations.literal: After long service in the headquarters he was made General of the Dragon Cavalry and Vice Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After long service in the headquarters he was appointed General of the Dragon Cavalry and Vice Director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，蕭衍遣將裴邃等寇淮南。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang, Xiao Yan sent the generals Pei Sui and others to raid Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiaochang era, Xiao Yan of Liang sent the generals Pei Sui and others to raid Huainan.

sentences.zh: 詔行臺酈道元、都督河間王琛討之，停師城父，累月不進。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the mobile headquarters of Li Daoyuan and the commander-in-chief, the Prince of Hejian Chen, to attack them; they halted the army at Chengfu and for many months did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the mobile headquarters of Li Daoyuan and the commander-in-chief, the Prince of Hejian Chen, to attack them, but they halted the army at Chengfu and for many months did not advance.

sentences.zh: 敕孝芬持節齎齊庫刀，[3]催令赴接，賊退而還。

translations.literal: An imperial order directed Xiaofen, bearing the staff and carrying the saber from the Qi arsenal, [3] to hurry and join the relief; the bandits retreated and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order directed Xiaofen, bearing the staff and carrying the saber from the Qi arsenal, [3] to hurry and join the relief force; the enemy retreated and he returned.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史李神儁為蕭衍遣將攻圍，詔加孝芬通直散騎常侍，以將軍為荊州刺史，兼尚書南道行臺，領軍司，率諸將以援神儁，因代焉。

translations.literal: Li Shenjun, Governor of Jing Province, was besieged by generals sent by Xiao Yan; an edict additionally made Xiaofen Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Scattered Cavalry, and with the rank of general made him Governor of Jing Province and concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing on the Southern Route Mobile Headquarters, commanding the army bureau and leading the generals to rescue Shenjun, thereby replacing him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenjun, Governor of Jing Province, was besieged by generals sent by Xiao Yan. An edict additionally appointed Xiaofen Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Scattered Cavalry, made him Governor of Jing Province with the rank of general, and assigned him as concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing on the Southern Route Mobile Headquarters, commanding the army bureau and leading the generals to rescue Shenjun, thereby replacing him.

sentences.zh: 於時，州郡內戍悉已陷沒，且路由三鵶，賊已先據。

translations.literal: At the time the garrisons within the province and commanderies had all fallen, and moreover the route passed through Sanyu, which the bandits had already seized first.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the garrisons within the province and commanderies had all fallen, and moreover the route passed through Sanyu, which the enemy had already seized.

sentences.zh: 孝芬所統既少，不得徑進，遂從弘農堰渠山道南入，遣弟孝直輕兵在前，出賊不意，賊便奔散，人還安堵。

translations.literal: The forces Xiaofen commanded were few and he could not advance directly, so he entered by the Hongnong canal and mountain road to the south, sent his younger brother Xiaozhi ahead with light troops, caught the bandits unawares, and the bandits at once fled and scattered; the people returned to peace.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaofen's forces were few and he could not advance directly, so he entered by the Hongnong canal and mountain road to the south and sent his younger brother Xiaozhi ahead with light troops. Catching the enemy unawares, he put them to flight and restored peace to the people.

sentences.zh: 肅宗嘉勞之，并賚馬及綿絹等物。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong praised and rewarded him, also bestowing horses, silk floss, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong praised and rewarded him, also bestowing horses, silk floss, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 後以元叉之黨，與盧同、李奬等並除名，徵還。

translations.literal: Later, because he was a partisan of Yuan Cha, together with Lu Tong, Li Jiang, and others he was struck from the rolls and summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because he was a partisan of Yuan Cha, he was struck from the rolls together with Lu Tong, Li Jiang, and others and summoned back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 又孝芬為廷尉之日，章武王融以贓貨被劾，孝芬按以重法。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Xiaofen was Vice Director of the Court of Justice, the Prince of Zhangwu Rong was impeached for bribery, and Xiaofen prosecuted him under the heavy law.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when Xiaofen served as Vice Director of the Court of Justice, the Prince of Zhangwu Rong was impeached for bribery, and Xiaofen prosecuted him under the heavy law.

sentences.zh: 及融為都督，北討鮮于脩禮，於時孝芬弟孝演率勒宗從，避賊於博陵，郡城為賊攻陷，尋為賊所害。

translations.literal: When Rong became commander-in-chief and campaigned north against Xianyu Xiuli, at that time Xiaofen's younger brother Xiaoyan led the clan kindred to avoid the bandits at Boling; the commandery city was taken by bandits, and soon he was killed by them.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong became commander-in-chief and campaigned north against Xianyu Xiuli, Xiaofen's younger brother Xiaoyan led the clan kindred to Boling to escape the rebels. The commandery city fell to the enemy, and Xiaoyan was soon killed.

sentences.zh: 融乃密啟，云：「孝演入賊為王。」

translations.literal: Rong then sent a secret memorial saying: "Xiaoyan entered the bandits and became their king."
translations.idiomatic: Rong then sent a secret memorial stating, "Xiaoyan joined the rebels and became their king."

sentences.zh: 遂見收捕，合家逃竄，遇赦乃出。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was arrested; the whole family fled and hid, and only after an amnesty did they emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the family was arrested; the whole household fled and hid, and only after an amnesty did they emerge.

sentences.zh: 孝昌三年，蕭衍將成景儁率眾逼彭城，除孝芬寧朔將軍、員外常侍、兼尚書右丞，為徐州行臺。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaochang, the Liang general Cheng Jingjun led troops to press Pengcheng; Xiaofen was made General Who Pacifies the North, Extraordinary Attendant, and concurrent Right Director of the Masters of Writing, and made Mobile Headquarters of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiaochang, the Liang general Cheng Jingjun led troops against Pengcheng. Xiaofen was appointed General Who Pacifies the North, Extraordinary Attendant, and concurrent Right Director of the Masters of Writing, and assigned to the mobile headquarters of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 孝芬將發，入辭。

translations.literal: As Xiaofen was about to set out, he entered to take leave.
translations.idiomatic: As Xiaofen was about to set out, he entered the palace to take leave.

sentences.zh: 靈太后謂孝芬曰：「卿女今事我兒，與卿便是親舊，曾何相負而內頭元叉車中，稱此老嫗會須却之。」

translations.literal: Empress Ling said to Cui Xiaofen: "Your daughter now serves my son; with you we are already kin and old friends—how have I wronged you, that privately in Yuan Cha's carriage he said this old hag will surely be removed?"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Ling said to Cui Xiaofen, "Your daughter now serves my son, so you and I are already kin. How have I wronged you, that Yuan Cha said privately, in his carriage, that this old woman would surely be removed?"

sentences.zh: 孝芬曰：「臣蒙國厚恩，義無斯語。

translations.literal: Cui Xiaofen said: "Your subject has received the state's great kindness; in principle there are no such words.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xiaofen replied, "Your subject has received the state's deep favor. Such words are utterly unthinkable.

sentences.zh: 假實有此，誰能得聞？

translations.literal: Even if there truly were this, who could have heard it?
translations.idiomatic: Even if such words were truly spoken, who could have overheard them?

sentences.zh: 若有聞知，此於元叉親密過臣遠矣。

translations.literal: If someone did hear and know of it, that person would be far closer to Yuan Cha in intimacy than I.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone did hear them, that person would be far more intimate with Yuan Cha than I am.

sentences.zh: 乞對言者，足辨虛實。」

translations.literal: I beg to confront the speaker; that would suffice to distinguish false from true."
translations.idiomatic: I ask only to face the accuser—that would be enough to establish the truth."

sentences.zh: 靈太后悵然意解，乃有愧色。

translations.literal: Empress Ling, moved and her understanding cleared, then showed a look of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Ling, softened and convinced, showed a look of shame.

sentences.zh: 景儁築柵造堰，謀斷泗水以灌彭城。

translations.literal: Cheng Jingjun built palisades and constructed a dam, planning to cut off the Si River to flood Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Jingjun built fortifications and a dam, intending to divert the Si River and flood Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 孝芬率大都督李叔仁、柴集等赴戰，[4]景儁等力屈退走。

translations.literal: Cui Xiaofen led the grand commander Li Shuren, Chai Ji, and others to battle; [4] Cheng Jingjun and the others, their strength exhausted, withdrew and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xiaofen led Grand Commander Li Shuren, Chai Ji, and others into battle; [4] Cheng Jingjun's forces, exhausted, withdrew in defeat.

sentences.zh: 除孝芬安南將軍、光祿大夫、兼尚書，為徐兗行臺。

translations.literal: Cui Xiaofen was made General Who Pacifies the South, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and concurrent Master of Writing, and assigned as Mobile Headquarters of Xu and Yan provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xiaofen was appointed General Who Pacifies the South, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and concurrent Master of Writing, with charge of the mobile headquarters for Xu and Yan provinces.

sentences.zh: 建義初，太山太守羊侃據郡反，遠引南賊，圍逼兗州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi, Yang Kan, Administrator of Mount Tai, held the commandery in rebellion, drawing in southern bandits from afar and besieging Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianyi era, Yang Kan, Administrator of Mount Tai, seized the commandery in revolt, summoned southern invaders from afar, and pressed Yan Province under siege.

sentences.zh: 除孝芬散騎常侍、鎮東將軍、金紫光祿大夫，仍兼尚書東道行臺，大都督刁宣馳往救援，[5]與行臺于暉接，至便圍之。

translations.literal: Cui Xiaofen was made Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, still concurrent Eastern Route Mobile Headquarters of the Masters of Writing; the grand commander Diao Xuan raced to rescue; [5] he joined with the mobile headquarters commander Yu Hui, and upon arrival immediately besieged them.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xiaofen was appointed Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the golden seal and purple ribbon, while retaining his post as concurrent head of the Eastern Route Mobile Headquarters. Grand Commander Diao Xuan rushed to the rescue; [5] he linked up with Mobile Headquarters Commander Yu Hui and, upon arrival, immediately laid siege.

sentences.zh: 侃突圍奔蕭衍，餘悉平定。

translations.literal: Kan broke out and fled to Xiao Yan; the rest were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kan broke out of the encirclement and fled to Emperor Wu of Liang; the remainder were wholly pacified.

sentences.zh: 永安二年，莊帝聞元顥有內侵之計，敕孝芬南赴徐州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yong'an, Emperor Zhuang heard that Yuan Hao had plans to invade from within, and ordered Cui Xiaofen south to Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yong'an, Emperor Zhuang learned that Yuan Hao intended to invade from within and ordered Cui Xiaofen south to Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 顥遂潛師向考城，擒大都督、濟陰王暉業，乘勝徑進，遣其後軍都督侯暄守梁國城以為後援。

translations.literal: Hao then moved his army secretly toward Kaocheng, captured the grand commander and Prince of Jiyin, Hui Ye, pressed straight forward taking advantage of victory, and sent his rear-army commander Hou Xuan to hold Liang Kingdom city as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao then marched in secret toward Kaocheng, captured Grand Commander and Prince of Jiyin Hui Ye, pressed forward on the momentum of victory, and dispatched Rear-Army Commander Hou Xuan to hold the city of Liang Kingdom as his rear guard.

sentences.zh: 孝芬勒諸將馳往圍暄，恐顥遣援，乃急攻之，晝夜不息。

translations.literal: Cui Xiaofen urged the generals to race and besiege Xuan, fearing Hao would send relief, so he pressed the attack without cease day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xiaofen drove his generals to race and surround Hou Xuan. Fearing Yuan Hao would send reinforcements, he pressed the assault day and night without pause.

sentences.zh: 五日，暄遂突出，擒斬之，俘其卒三千餘人。

translations.literal: On the fifth day, Xuan broke out and was captured and executed; more than three thousand of his soldiers were taken prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day Hou Xuan broke out, was captured, and executed; more than three thousand of his troops were taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 莊帝還宮，授西兗州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, Cui Xiaofen was appointed Inspector of Western Yan Province, his generalship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the capital, Cui Xiaofen was appointed Inspector of Western Yan Province, retaining his rank as general.

sentences.zh: 孝芬久倦外役，固辭不行，乃除太常卿。

translations.literal: Cui Xiaofen, long weary of service abroad, firmly declined and would not go; he was then made Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xiaofen, long wearied by campaigns abroad, firmly declined the post and refused to go; he was instead appointed Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 普泰元年，南陽太守趙脩延襲據荊州城，囚刺史李琰之，招引南寇。

translations.literal: In the first year of Putai, Zhao Xiuyan, Administrator of Nanyang, seized and held Jing Province city, imprisoned the inspector Li Yanzhi, and summoned southern invaders.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Putai, Zhao Xiuyan, Administrator of Nanyang, seized Jing Province's capital by surprise, imprisoned Inspector Li Yanzhi, and called in southern raiders.

sentences.zh: 除孝芬衞將軍、荊州刺史，兼尚書南道行臺。

translations.literal: Cui Xiaofen was made General of the Guard, Inspector of Jing Province, and concurrent Southern Route Mobile Headquarters of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xiaofen was appointed General of the Guard, Inspector of Jing Province, and concurrent head of the Southern Route Mobile Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 又除都督三荊諸軍事、車騎將軍、假驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: He was further made Commander-in-Chief of the Military Affairs of the Three Jing Regions, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Acting General of Rapid Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the Three Jing Regions, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Acting General of Rapid Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 孝芬已出次，改授散騎常侍、驃騎將軍、西兗州刺史。

translations.literal: After Cui Xiaofen had already set out and encamped, he was reassigned as Regular Attendant, General of Rapid Cavalry, and Inspector of Western Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Cui Xiaofen had already marched out and encamped, he was reassigned as Regular Attendant, General of Rapid Cavalry, and Inspector of Western Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，兼殿中尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he was made concurrent Director of the Palace Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Taichang era, he was made concurrent Director of the Palace Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 尋除車騎大將軍、左光祿大夫，仍尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, still Master of Writing.
