translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, retaining his post in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 後加儀同三司、兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Later he was further given the Three Excellencies of Equal Rank and made concurrent Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was further granted the Three Excellencies of Equal Rank and appointed concurrent Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 出帝入關，齊獻武王至洛，與尚書辛雄、劉廞等並誅，時年五十。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor entered the pass, Prince Xianwu of Qi arrived at Luoyang, and Cui Xiaofen was executed together with the Masters of Writing Xin Xiong, Liu Yin, and others; he was fifty years old at the time.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor fled west into the pass, Prince Xianwu of Qi reached Luoyang. Cui Xiaofen was executed together with the Masters of Writing Xin Xiong, Liu Yin, and others. He was fifty years old.

sentences.zh: 沒其家口，天平中乃免之。

translations.literal: His household was confiscated; only in the Tianping era were they released.
translations.idiomatic: His household was confiscated; only during the Tianping era were they released from bondage.

sentences.zh: 孝芬博文口辯，善談論，愛好後進，終日忻然，商搉古今，間以嘲謔，聽者忘疲。

translations.literal: Cui Xiaofen was learned and eloquent, skilled at discussion, fond of nurturing juniors; all day he was joyful, weighing ancient and modern matters, intermittently mixing in mockery and jest—listeners forgot their fatigue.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xiaofen was learned and eloquent, a gifted conversationalist who loved to encourage younger men. All day long he was cheerful, debating past and present and now and then breaking into banter and jest, so that those who listened forgot their weariness.

sentences.zh: 所著文章數十篇。

translations.literal: The writings he composed numbered several tens of pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote several dozen essays.

sentences.zh: [6]有子八人。

translations.literal: [6] He had eight sons.
translations.idiomatic: [6] He had eight sons.

sentences.zh: 長子勉，字宣祖。

translations.literal: His eldest son Mian, courtesy name Xuanzu.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Mian, courtesy name Xuanzu.

sentences.zh: 頗涉史傳，有几案才。

translations.literal: He had considerable knowledge of history and the classics, and had talent for desk work.
translations.idiomatic: He was well versed in history and the classics and had a gift for administrative work.

sentences.zh: 正光初，除太學博士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengguang, he was made Doctor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhengguang era, he was appointed Doctor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 莊帝之為御史中尉，啟除侍御史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang was Censor-in-Chief, he petitioned to appoint him Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang served as Censor-in-Chief, he petitioned to have Mian appointed Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 永安初，除建節將軍、尚書右中兵郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an, he was made General Who Establishes Military Authority and Right Director of the Central Military Section of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yong'an era, he was appointed General Who Establishes Military Authority and Right Director of the Central Military Section in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 後太尉、豫章王蕭贊啟為諮議參軍，郎中如故。

translations.literal: Later the Grand Marshal and Prince of Yuzhang, Xiao Zan, petitioned to appoint him as Staff Adviser; his directorship remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Later Grand Marshal and Prince of Yuzhang Xiao Zan petitioned to appoint him Staff Adviser, while he retained his post as director.

sentences.zh: 以舉人失衷，為中尉高道穆奏免其官。

translations.literal: Because his recommendation of personnel missed the mark, the Censor-in-Chief Gao Daomu memorialized and had him dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Because his recommendations of personnel had missed the mark, Censor-in-Chief Gao Daomu memorialized for his dismissal from office.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，兼尚書左丞。

translations.literal: In the Putai era, he was made concurrent Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Putai era, he was appointed concurrent Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 勉善附會，世論以浮競譏之。

translations.literal: Mian was good at currying favor; public opinion criticized him as flashy and competitive.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was skilled at currying favor, and public opinion mocked him as shallow and ambitious.

sentences.zh: 為尚書令尒朱世隆所親待，而尚書郎魏季景尤為世隆知任，勉與季景內頗不穆。

translations.literal: He was favored and treated warmly by the Master of Writing Erzhu Shilong, but the Master of Writing Attendant Wei Jijing was especially trusted by Shilong; Mian and Jijing were inwardly quite estranged.
translations.idiomatic: He was favored by Master of Writing Erzhu Shilong, but Master of Writing Attendant Wei Jijing enjoyed Shilong's trust above all others; inwardly Mian and Jijing were deeply at odds.

sentences.zh: 季景陰求右丞，奪勉所兼。

translations.literal: Jijing secretly sought the vice directorship and wrested from Mian his concurrent post.
translations.idiomatic: Jijing secretly sought the vice directorship and stripped Mian of his concurrent appointment.

sentences.zh: 世隆啟用季景，勉遂悵怏自失。

translations.literal: Shilong petitioned to appoint Jijing; Mian then felt resentful and lost.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong petitioned to appoint Jijing, and Mian, resentful and dispirited, fell into despondency.

sentences.zh: 尋除安南將軍、光祿大夫、兼國子祭酒，典儀注。

translations.literal: Soon he was made General Who Pacifies the South, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and concurrent Rector of the National University, overseeing ritual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and concurrent Rector of the National University, with charge of ritual protocol.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，除散騎常侍、征東將軍、金紫光祿大夫、定州大中正，敕左右廂出入其家。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he was made Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Chief Rectifier of Ding Province; an edict allowed the left and right guard posts to pass through his household.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Taichang era, he was appointed Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the golden seal and purple ribbon, and Chief Rectifier of Ding Province; an edict permitted the left and right guard posts to pass through his household.

sentences.zh: 被收之際，在外逃免。

translations.literal: At the time of his family's arrest, he escaped abroad.
translations.idiomatic: When the arrests came, he was abroad and escaped capture.

sentences.zh: 於後乃出，見齊獻武王於晉陽，王勞撫之。

translations.literal: Only afterward did he come forth and saw Prince Xianwu of Qi at Jinyang; the prince comforted and supported him.
translations.idiomatic: Only afterward did he emerge and present himself to Prince Xianwu of Qi at Jinyang; the prince received him with kindness and reassurance.

sentences.zh: 天平末，王遣勉送勳貴妻子赴定州，因得還家。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianping, the prince sent Mian to escort the wives and children of meritorious nobles to Ding Province, and thereby he was able to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Tianping era, the prince sent Mian to escort the wives and children of meritorious nobles to Ding Province, and in that way he was able to return home.

sentences.zh: 屬母李氏喪亡，勉哀號過性，遇病卒，時年四十七。

translations.literal: When his mother Lady Li died, Mian wailed beyond all bounds of nature, fell ill, and died; he was forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother Lady Li died, Mian mourned with a grief that exceeded all natural bounds, fell ill, and died at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟宣度以子龍後之。

translations.literal: He had no sons; his younger brother Xuandu made his son Long the heir.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons; his younger brother Xuandu adopted his son Long as Mian's heir.

sentences.zh: 勉弟宣猷，司徒中郎，走於關西。

translations.literal: Mian's younger brother Xuanyou was a Gentleman of the Secretariat; he fled to the western passes.
translations.idiomatic: Mian's younger brother Xuanyou served as Gentleman of the Secretariat and fled to the western passes.

sentences.zh: 宣猷弟宣度，齊王儀同開府司馬。

translations.literal: Xuanyou's younger brother Xuandu was Assistant Master of the Princely Establishment of Equal Rank with the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanyou's younger brother Xuandu served as Assistant Master of the Prince of Qi's Establishment of Equal Rank.

sentences.zh: 宣度弟宣軌，頗有才學。

translations.literal: Xuandu's younger brother Xuangui had considerable talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Xuandu's younger brother Xuangui was a man of considerable talent and learning.

sentences.zh: 尚書考功郎中。

translations.literal: Director of Merit Evaluation in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Director of Merit Evaluation in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 與弟宣質、宣靜、宣略，並死於晉陽。

translations.literal: Together with his younger brothers Xuanzhi, Xuanjing, and Xuanlüe, all died at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brothers Xuanzhi, Xuanjing, and Xuanlüe all died at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 孝芬弟孝暐，字敬業。

translations.literal: Cui Xiaofen's younger brother Xiaowei, courtesy name Jingye.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xiaofen's younger brother was Xiaowei, courtesy name Jingye.

sentences.zh: 少寬雅，早著長者之風。

translations.literal: In youth he was broadly refined; early on he showed the bearing of an elder.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was broad-minded and refined, and early on he showed the bearing of a man of mature character.

sentences.zh: 彭城王勰之臨定州，辟為主簿。

translations.literal: When Prince Xie of Pengcheng arrived in Ding Province, he recruited him as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xie of Pengcheng took up his post in Ding Province, he recruited Xiaowei as Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 釋褐冀州安東府外兵參軍，歷員外散騎侍郎、寧朔將軍、員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At his first appointment he was Outside Army Officer of the Pacifying East Headquarters of Ji Province, and passed through Extraordinary Attendant of the Loose Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the North, and Extraordinary Regular Attendant of the Loose Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering office he served as Outside Army Officer of the Pacifying East Headquarters in Ji Province, and later held the posts of Extraordinary Attendant of the Loose Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the North, and Extraordinary Regular Attendant of the Loose Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 武泰初，蠻首李洪扇動諸蠻，詔孝暐持節為別將，隸都督李神軌討平之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wutai, the Man chieftain Li Hong stirred up the various Man; an edict ordered Xiaowei to bear the staff as a separate commander under the commander-in-chief Li Shengui to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Wutai era, the Man chieftain Li Hong stirred up the various Man tribes. An edict ordered Xiaowei to bear the staff as a separate commander under Commander-in-Chief Li Shengui and suppress them.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮之害朝士，孝暐與弟孝直攜家避難定陶。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong killed the court officials, Xiaowei and his younger brother Xiaozhi took their families to flee to Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong slaughtered the court officials, Xiaowei and his younger brother Xiaozhi took their families and fled to Dingtao for refuge.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，徵拜通直散騎常侍，加征虜將軍，尋除趙郡太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, he was summoned and appointed Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, with the additional title General Who Repels the Barbarians; soon he was made Administrator of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, he was summoned and appointed Regular Attendant of Direct Communication with the additional rank of General Who Repels the Barbarians; soon afterward he was made Administrator of Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 郡經葛榮離亂之後，民戶喪亡，六畜無遺，斗粟乃至數縑，民皆賣鬻兒女。

translations.literal: The commandery had suffered the chaos of Ge Rong's devastation; households were destroyed, not a single head of livestock remained, a peck of grain cost even several bolts of silk, and the people all sold their sons and daughters.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery had been ravaged by Ge Rong's upheaval: households were wiped out, not a single head of livestock remained, and a peck of grain could cost several bolts of silk. The people were selling their sons and daughters.

sentences.zh: 夏椹大熟，孝暐勸民多收之。

translations.literal: When the summer mulberries ripened greatly, Xiaowei urged the people to gather them in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: When the summer mulberries ripened in abundance, Xiaowei urged the people to gather as many as they could.

sentences.zh: 郡內無牛，教其人種。

translations.literal: Within the commandery there were no oxen; he taught the people to cultivate by hand.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery had no oxen, so he taught the people to plow and plant by hand.

sentences.zh: 招撫遺散，先恩後威，一周之後，流民大至。

translations.literal: He summoned and comforted the scattered refugees, favor first and severity afterward; within a week, displaced people came in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned and reassured the scattered refugees, showing kindness before severity. Within a week displaced people came flooding in.

sentences.zh: 興立學校，親加勸篤，百姓賴之。

translations.literal: He established schools and personally urged and encouraged them; the common people relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: He founded schools and personally encouraged learning; the people came to depend on him.

sentences.zh: 卒於郡，時年四十九。

translations.literal: He died in the commandery; he was forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the commandery at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈通直散騎常侍、平東將軍、瀛州刺史，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: Posthumously given Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, General Who Pacifies the East, and Inspector of Ying Province; posthumous name Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the ranks of Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, General Who Pacifies the East, and Inspector of Ying Province, with the posthumous name Jian.

sentences.zh: 朝議謂為未申，復贈安北將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Court discussion held this insufficient; he was again given posthumously General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion held that this was insufficient, and he was posthumously granted the additional ranks of General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 子昂，武定中，尚書左丞、兼度支尚書。

translations.literal: His son Ang, in the Wuding era, was Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and concurrent Minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ang, during the Wuding era, served as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and concurrent Minister of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 孝暐弟孝演，字則伯，出繼伯父。

translations.literal: Xiaowei's younger brother Xiaoyan, courtesy name Zebo, was adopted as heir to his paternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowei's younger brother was Xiaoyan, courtesy name Zebo, who had been adopted as heir to his paternal uncle.

sentences.zh: 性通率，美鬚髯，姿貌魁傑。

translations.literal: By nature he was straightforward; fine beard and eyebrows; imposing stature.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was frank and unpretentious, with a fine beard and imposing, heroic bearing.

sentences.zh: 少無宦情，沉浮鄉里。

translations.literal: In youth he had no taste for office; he drifted in his native district.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had no taste for official life and drifted quietly in his home district.

sentences.zh: 河間王琛為定州刺史，以為治中。

translations.literal: When Prince Chen of Hejian was Inspector of Ding Province, he made him Administrative Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chen of Hejian served as Inspector of Ding Province, he appointed Xiaoyan Administrative Adviser.

sentences.zh: 晚除瀛州安西府外兵參軍，因罷歸。

translations.literal: Only late in life was he made Outside Army Officer of the Pacifying West Headquarters of Ying Province; he then resigned and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Only late in life was he appointed Outside Army Officer of the Pacifying West Headquarters in Ying Province; he then resigned and returned home.

sentences.zh: 及鮮于脩禮起逆，孝演率宗屬保郡城，為賊攻陷。

translations.literal: When Xianyu Xiuli rose in rebellion, Xiaoyan led the clan to hold the commandery city; it was overrun by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianyu Xiuli rose in rebellion, Xiaoyan led the clan to defend the commandery city, but it was overrun by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊以孝演民望，恐移眾心，乃害之，時年四十。

translations.literal: The bandits, because Xiaoyan had standing among the people, feared he would sway the masses' hearts, so they killed him; he was forty.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xiaoyan enjoyed standing among the people, the rebels feared he would turn popular sentiment against them and killed him. He was forty years old.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟孝直以子士遊為後。

translations.literal: He had no sons; his younger brother Xiaozhi made his son Shiyou the heir.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons; his younger brother Xiaozhi adopted his son Shiyou as Xiaoyan's heir.

sentences.zh: 士遊，儀同開府倉曹參軍。

translations.literal: Shiyou was Record-keeping Officer of the Princely Establishment of Equal Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyou served as Record-keeping Officer of an Establishment of Equal Rank.

sentences.zh: 孝演弟孝直，字叔廉。

translations.literal: Xiaoyan's younger brother Xiaozhi, courtesy name Shulian.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyan's younger brother was Xiaozhi, courtesy name Shulian.

sentences.zh: 身八尺，眉目踈朗。

translations.literal: Eight feet in height; eyebrows and eyes sparse and clear-bright.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight feet tall, with sparse, clear-bright brows and eyes.

sentences.zh: 早有志尚，起家司空行參軍。

translations.literal: Early on he had lofty aspirations; he began his career as Master of Protocol of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: From early on he had lofty aspirations and began his career as Master of Protocol under the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 尋為員外散騎侍郎、宣威將，[7]仍以本官入領直後。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Extraordinary Attendant of the Loose Cavalry and General Who Proclaims Majesty; [7] still with his original office he entered to head the Palace Guard Rear.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Extraordinary Attendant of the Loose Cavalry and General Who Proclaims Majesty; [7] retaining his original rank, he entered palace service as head of the Palace Guard Rear.

sentences.zh: 轉寧遠將軍、汝南王開府掾，領直寢。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of Distant Service and Staff Officer of the Princely Establishment of the Prince of Runan, heading the Palace Guard Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General of Distant Service and staff officer on the Prince of Runan's establishment, with charge of the Palace Guard Chamber.

sentences.zh: 兄孝芬除荊州，詔孝直假征虜將軍，別將，總羽林二千騎，與孝芬俱行。

translations.literal: When his elder brother Cui Xiaofen was made Inspector of Jing Province, an edict appointed Xiaozhi Acting General Who Repels the Barbarians and Separate Commander, commanding two thousand Household Guard cavalry, and traveling together with Cui Xiaofen.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother Cui Xiaofen was appointed Inspector of Jing Province, an edict named Xiaozhi Acting General Who Repels the Barbarians and Separate Commander, commanding two thousand Household Guard cavalry, to march with Cui Xiaofen.

sentences.zh: 孝直潛師徑進，賊遂破走。

translations.literal: Xiaozhi moved his army by a secret route straight forward; the bandits were broken and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhi marched by a secret route straight at the enemy, and the rebels were broken and put to flight.

sentences.zh: 孝芬入城後，蕭衍將曹義宗仍在馬圈，鼓動順陽蠻夷，緣邊寇竊。

translations.literal: After Cui Xiaofen entered the city, Xiao Yan's general Cao Yizong still remained at Maquan, stirring up the Shunyang barbarians and border peoples to raid and plunder along the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: After Cui Xiaofen entered the city, Emperor Wu of Liang's general Cao Yizong still held Maquan, inciting the Shunyang barbarians and frontier peoples to raid along the border.

sentences.zh: 孝直率眾禦之，賊皆退散。

translations.literal: Xiaozhi led troops to repel them; the bandits all retreated and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhi led his troops to repel them, and the raiders all withdrew and dispersed.

sentences.zh: 還轉直閤將軍、通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: On return he was transferred to General of the Palace Guard and Regular Attendant of Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his return he was transferred to General of the Palace Guard and Regular Attendant of Direct Communication.

sentences.zh: 尒朱兆入洛，孝直以天下未寧，去職歸鄉里，勸督宗人，務行禮義。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Xiaozhi, because the realm was not yet settled, left office and returned to his native district, exhorting and supervising the clan to devote themselves to ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Xiaozhi, seeing that the realm was still unsettled, resigned and returned to his home district, urging and guiding his clansmen to observe ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 後除安東將軍、光祿大夫，太昌中，又除衞將軍、右光祿大夫，並辭不赴。

translations.literal: Later he was made General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; in the Taichang era he was again made General of the Guard and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness—all declined without going.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; during the Taichang era he was again offered the posts of General of the Guard and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness—all of which he declined.

sentences.zh: 宗親勸孝直曰：「榮華人之所願，何故陸沉？」

translations.literal: Kinsmen urged Xiaozhi: "Glory and splendor are what people desire—why do you sink into obscurity?"
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen urged Xiaozhi, "Glory and honor are what every man desires—why do you bury yourself in obscurity?"

sentences.zh: 孝直不答。

translations.literal: Xiaozhi did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhi did not reply.

sentences.zh: 年五十八，卒於鄉里，顧命諸子曰：「吾才疏效薄，於國無功，若朝廷復加贈諡，宜循吾意，不得祗受，若致干求，則非吾子，斂以時服，祭勿殺生。」

translations.literal: At fifty-eight he died in his native district; he gave final instructions to his sons: "My talent is meager and my achievements slight; I have been without merit to the state. If the court again adds posthumous honors, you should follow my wishes and must not respectfully accept them. If you importune for them, then you are not my sons. Bury me in timely dress; at sacrifices do not kill living creatures."
translations.idiomatic: At the age of fifty-eight he died in his home district. He gave his final instructions to his sons: "My talent is slight and my achievements meager; I have done nothing for the state. If the court should again offer posthumous honors, you must follow my wishes and refuse them. If you petition for such honors, you are no sons of mine. Bury me in ordinary dress, and at sacrifices do not kill living creatures."

sentences.zh: 其子皆遵行之。

translations.literal: His sons all obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: His sons all obeyed.

sentences.zh: 有四子。

translations.literal: He had four sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons.

sentences.zh: 長子士順，儀同開府行參軍。

translations.literal: His eldest son Shishun was Master of Protocol of the Princely Establishment of Equal Rank.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Shishun served as Master of Protocol of an Establishment of Equal Rank.

sentences.zh: 孝直弟孝政，字季讓。

translations.literal: Xiaozhi's younger brother Xiaozheng, courtesy name Jirang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhi's younger brother was Xiaozheng, courtesy name Jirang.

sentences.zh: 十歲，挺亡，號哭不絕，見者為之悲傷。

translations.literal: At ten, when Ting died, he wailed without cease; those who saw it were moved to sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of ten, when Cui Ting died, he wailed without stopping; all who saw him were moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 操尚貞立，博洽經史，雅好辭賦。

translations.literal: His conduct prized integrity and uprightness; he was broadly versed in the classics and histories and fond of poetry and rhapsodies in elegant taste.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct prized integrity and uprightness; he was broadly versed in the classics and histories and had an elegant love of poetry and rhapsody.

sentences.zh: 喪紀之禮，特所留情，衣服制度，手能執造。

translations.literal: The rites of mourning were what he especially devoted himself to; regulations for vestments and ritual dress he could personally craft with his own hands.
translations.idiomatic: He took particular care with the rites of mourning, and could personally cut and sew the prescribed vestments and ritual dress.

sentences.zh: 太尉、汝南王悅辟行參軍。

translations.literal: The Defender-in-Chief, the Prince of Runan Yue, recruited him as Traveling Aide.
translations.idiomatic: The Defender-in-Chief, Prince Yue of Runan, recruited him as a staff officer on his establishment.

sentences.zh: 年四十九，卒。

translations.literal: At forty-nine he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子巖，武定中，員外常侍。

translations.literal: His son Yan, in the Wuding era, was Extraordinary Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan served as Extraordinary Regular Attendant during the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 孝芬兄弟孝義慈厚，弟孝演、孝政先亡，孝芬等哭泣哀慟，絕內，蔬食，容貌損瘠，見者傷之。

translations.literal: The brothers Xiaofen were filial, righteous, kind, and generous; their younger brothers Xiaoyan and Xiaozheng died first, and Xiaofen and the others wept and wailed in deepest grief, abstained from relations with their wives, ate only vegetables, their appearances wasted and gaunt—those who saw them were moved to sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiaofen brothers were filial, benevolent, and generous in spirit. When their younger brothers Xiaoyan and Xiaozheng died first, Xiaofen and the others wept in anguish, abstained from their wives, ate only plain food, and grew gaunt and wasted in appearance. All who saw them were moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 孝暐等奉孝芬盡恭順之禮，坐食進退，孝芬不命則不敢也。

translations.literal: Xiaowei and the others observed toward Xiaofen the utmost rites of reverence and obedience; in sitting, eating, advancing, and retreating, if Xiaofen did not command, they did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowei and the others treated Xiaofen with the utmost reverence and obedience. In sitting down, eating, or coming and going, they would not act unless Xiaofen directed them.

sentences.zh: 鷄鳴而起，旦參顏色，一錢尺帛，不入私房，吉凶有須，聚對分給。

translations.literal: At cockcrow they rose, and at dawn inquired after his complexion; not a cash's worth nor a foot of silk entered their private rooms—when fortune or misfortune required expenses, they gathered and apportioned them among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They rose at cockcrow and each morning inquired after his health. Not a single coin or inch of silk went into their private stores; whenever expenses for festive or mournful occasions arose, they pooled resources and divided them among themselves.

sentences.zh: 諸婦亦相親愛，有無共之。

translations.literal: The wives too mutually loved one another and shared what they had or had not.
translations.idiomatic: The wives also loved one another dearly and shared whatever they had.

sentences.zh: 始挺兄弟同居，孝芬叔振既亡之後，孝芬等奉承叔母李氏，若事所生，旦夕溫凊，出入啟覲，家事巨細，一以諮決。

translations.literal: From the beginning the brothers of the Ting line lived together; after their father's younger brother Zhen had died, Xiaofen and the others served their aunt by marriage Lady Li as though she were their birth mother, morning and evening tending to her warmth and coolness, on going out and returning reporting and paying respects; in household affairs great and small, all were decided only after consulting her.
translations.idiomatic: The Cui Ting brothers had lived together from the start. After their uncle Zhen died, Xiaofen and the others cared for their aunt, Lady Li, as though she were their own mother—attending to her comfort morning and evening, reporting to her whenever they came or went, and consulting her on every matter of household affairs, great or small.

sentences.zh: 每兄弟出行，有獲財物，尺寸已上，皆內李氏之庫，四時分賚，李自裁之，如此者二十餘歲。

translations.literal: Whenever the brothers went out and obtained goods or wealth, items of even a foot or more in measure, all were deposited in Lady Li's storehouse; at the four seasons they were allotted as gifts, and Li herself decided the distributions—this continued for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the brothers went out and acquired goods, even the smallest items were placed in Lady Li's storeroom. Season after season she distributed them as gifts at her own discretion, and this continued for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 撫從弟宣伯子朗，如同氣焉。

translations.literal: He raised his younger cousin Xuanbo's son Lang as though of the same breath.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his younger cousin Xuanbo's son Lang as though he were his own brother.

sentences.zh: 挺弟振，字延根。

translations.literal: Ting's younger brother Zhen, courtesy name Yangen.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ting's younger brother was Zhen, courtesy name Yangen.

sentences.zh: 少有學行，居家孝友，為宗族所稱。

translations.literal: In youth he had learning and conduct; at home he was filial and friendly, and was praised by the clan.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed learning and integrity. Filial and amiable at home, he was praised throughout the clan.

sentences.zh: 自中書學生為祕書中散，在內謹敕，為高祖所知。

translations.literal: From student of the Central Secretariat he became Palace Attendant of the Secretariat; within the palace he was careful and disciplined, and was noticed by Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a student of the Central Secretariat, he became Palace Attendant of the Secretariat. Diligent and disciplined within the palace, he came to Emperor Gaozu's attention.

sentences.zh: 出為冀州、咸陽王禧驃騎府司馬，在任久之。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief Administrator of the Rapid Cavalry Headquarters of the Prince of Xianyang Xi in Ji Province, and served long in his post.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as Chief Administrator of the Rapid Cavalry Headquarters of Prince Xi of Xianyang in Ji Province, and remained in that post for a long time.

sentences.zh: 太和二十年，遷建威將軍、平陽太守。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Taihe he was transferred to General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Taihe he was promoted to General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 不拜，轉高陽內史。

translations.literal: He did not accept the appointment and was transferred to Inner Magistrate of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the appointment and was transferred to Inner Magistrate of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖南討，徵兼尚書左丞，留京。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu campaigned south, he was summoned as Concurrent Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing and remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu marched south on campaign, Zhen was summoned to serve concurrently as Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing and was left in the capital.

sentences.zh: 振既才幹被擢，當世以為榮。

translations.literal: Since Zhen's talent and ability had been elevated, his contemporaries regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhen had been promoted for his talent and ability, his contemporaries regarded it as a distinction.

sentences.zh: 後改定職令，振本資惟擬五品，詔曰：「振在郡著績，宜有褒升。」

translations.literal: Later when official ranks were reformed and fixed, Zhen's original qualification would only have placed him in the fifth rank; an edict said: "Zhen has shown achievement in the commandery and should receive commendation and promotion."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the official rank system was reformed, Zhen's original qualification would have placed him only in the fifth rank. An edict stated: "Zhen has achieved distinction in his commandery and deserves commendation and promotion."

sentences.zh: 除太子庶子。

translations.literal: He was made Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 景明初，除長兼廷尉少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming he was made Senior Concurrent Vice Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingming era he was appointed Senior Concurrent Vice Director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 振有公斷，以明察稱。

translations.literal: Zhen had fair judgment and was known for keen discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was known for fair judgment and keen discernment.

sentences.zh: 河內太守陸琇與咸陽王禧同謀為逆，禧敗事發，振窮治之。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Henei Lu Qiu conspired with the Prince of Xianyang Xi to rebel; when Xi's plot failed and the matter came to light, Zhen thoroughly prosecuted him.
translations.idiomatic: When Henei Administrator Lu Qiu conspired with Prince Xi of Xianyang to rebel, and Xi's plot collapsed, Zhen prosecuted the case with exhaustive thoroughness.

sentences.zh: 時琇內外親黨及當朝貴要咸為之言，振研覈切至，終無縱緩，遂斃之於獄。

translations.literal: At the time Qiu's relatives inside and outside and the powerful figures of the court all spoke on his behalf, but Zhen's investigation was thorough and incisive; in the end he showed no leniency and had him beaten to death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Qiu's kin and the court's powerful figures all interceded on his behalf, but Zhen's investigation was exhaustive and unsparing. Showing no leniency, he had Qiu beaten to death in prison.

sentences.zh: 其奉法如此。

translations.literal: Such was his adherence to the law.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his devotion to the law.

sentences.zh: 正始初，除龍驤將軍、肆州刺史，在任有政績。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengshi he was made General of the Dragon Cavalry and Inspector of Si Province; in office he had administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhengshi era he was appointed General of the Dragon Cavalry and Inspector of Si Province, where he achieved notable results in office.

sentences.zh: 還朝，除河東太守。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he was made Administrator of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to court, he was appointed Administrator of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 永平中，卒於郡，時年五十九。

translations.literal: In the Yongping era he died in the commandery, at the age of fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongping era he died in office at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈本將軍、南兗州刺史，諡曰定。

translations.literal: Posthumously given his former rank of general and Inspector of Southern Yan Province; posthumous name Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored with his former rank of general and as Inspector of Southern Yan Province; his posthumous name was Ding.

sentences.zh: 振歷官四十餘載，考課恒為稱職。

translations.literal: Zhen held office for more than forty years; in merit evaluations he was constantly rated as fulfilling his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen served in office for more than forty years, and in merit evaluations he was consistently rated as fulfilling his duties.

sentences.zh: 議者善之。

translations.literal: Commentators approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Those who discussed the matter praised it.

sentences.zh: 長子宣伯，早喪。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xuanbo died early.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Xuanbo died prematurely.

sentences.zh: 子勁，字仲括。

translations.literal: His son Jin, courtesy name Zhongkuo.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jin, courtesy name Zhongkuo.

sentences.zh: 驃騎參軍。

translations.literal: Aide of the Rapid Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He served as aide on a Rapid Cavalry staff.

sentences.zh: 宣伯弟子朗，美容貌，涉獵經史，少溫厚，有風尚。

translations.literal: Xuanbo's younger brother's son Lang had a handsome appearance, ranged broadly through the classics and histories, in youth was warm and generous, and had moral bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbo's nephew Lang was handsome in appearance, widely read in the classics and histories, gentle and generous from youth, and possessed a cultivated moral bearing.

sentences.zh: 以軍功起家襄威將軍、員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: By military merit he began his career as General Who Displays Martiality and Extraordinary Attendant of the Loose Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office through military merit as General Who Displays Martiality and Extraordinary Attendant of the Loose Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，從兄孝芬為荊州，請為車騎府司馬。

translations.literal: In Putai, when his older cousin Xiaofen became Inspector of Jing Province, he requested Lang as Chief Administrator of the Chariots and Cavalry Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: During the Putai era, when his older cousin Xiaofen became Inspector of Jing Province, he invited Lang to serve as Chief Administrator of his Chariots and Cavalry Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 孝芬轉西兗州，為驃騎府司馬。

translations.literal: When Xiaofen was transferred to Western Yan Province, Lang became Chief Administrator of the Rapid Cavalry Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaofen was transferred to Western Yan Province, Lang served as Chief Administrator of his Rapid Cavalry Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，冠軍將軍、北徐州撫軍府長史，固辭，不獲免。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was Champion General and Chief Clerk of the Pacification Army headquarters of Northern Xu Province; he firmly declined but could not be excused.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Taichang era he was appointed Champion General and Chief Clerk of the Pacification Army headquarters in Northern Xu Province. He firmly declined but could not secure a release from the appointment.

sentences.zh: 興和二年，中尉高仲密引為侍御史，尋加平西將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xinghe, the Censor-in-Chief Gao Zhongmi brought him in as Attending Censor; soon he was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xinghe, Censor-in-Chief Gao Zhongmi brought him in as Attending Censor, and soon afterward he was granted the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 武定中卒。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 子道綱。

translations.literal: His son Daogang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Daogang.

sentences.zh: 挺從父弟元珍，釋褐司徒行參軍，稍遷司徒主簿、趙郡王幹開府屬。

translations.literal: Ting's father's younger brother's son Yuanzhen, at his first appointment was Traveling Aide of the Minister of Education; gradually he was promoted to Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education and Member of the Princely Establishment of the Prince of Zhao Commandery Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Ting's paternal cousin Yuanzhen entered office as a staff officer under the Minister of Education, then gradually rose to Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education and a member of Prince Gan of Zhao Commandery's princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 景明中，荊州長史。

translations.literal: In the Jingming era he was Chief Clerk of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingming era he served as Chief Clerk of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 久之，為司徒從事中郎，有公平稱。

translations.literal: After a long time he became Attendant of the Minister of Education and was known for fairness.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed Attendant of the Minister of Education and earned a reputation for fairness.

sentences.zh: 後遷中散大夫，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Palace Attendant and given the additional title General Who Repels the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Palace Attendant with the additional rank of General Who Repels the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 正光末，山胡作逆，除平陽太守，假右將軍，為別將以討之，頻破胡賊，郡內以安。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengguang the Mountain Hu rebelled; he was made Administrator of Pingyang, provisionally General of the Right, and a separate commander to suppress them; repeatedly he defeated the Hu bandits and the commandery was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Zhengguang era, when the Mountain Hu rebelled, he was appointed Administrator of Pingyang and provisionally made General of the Right, serving as a separate commander to suppress them. He repeatedly defeated the Hu raiders and pacified the commandery.

sentences.zh: 武泰初，改郡為唐州，仍除元珍為刺史，加右將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wutai the commandery was changed to Tang Province; Yuanzhen was still made Inspector and given the additional title General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Wutai era the commandery was redesignated as Tang Province, and Yuanzhen was appointed its inspector with the additional rank of General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 以破胡勳，賜爵涼城侯。

translations.literal: For merit in defeating the Hu he was given the title Marquis of Liangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in defeating the Hu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Liangcheng.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮之趣洛也，遣其都督樊子鵠取唐州。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong pressed toward Luoyang, he sent his commander Fan Zihu to take Tang Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong marched on Luoyang, he dispatched his commander Fan Zihu to seize Tang Province.

sentences.zh: 元珍與行臺酈惲拒守不從，為子鵠所陷，被害。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen together with the Mobile Headquarters Li Yun held firm in defense and refused submission; he was trapped by Zihu and put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen and Mobile Headquarters Commissioner Li Yun held the city in defiance, but were outmaneuvered by Zihu and killed.

sentences.zh: 世咸痛之。

translations.literal: The age all grieved for him.
translations.idiomatic: All who knew of it mourned him.

sentences.zh: 子叔恭。

translations.literal: His son Shugong.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Shugong.

sentences.zh: 挺從父弟瑜之，字仲璉。

translations.literal: Ting's father's younger brother's son Yuzhi, courtesy name Zhonglian.
translations.idiomatic: Ting's paternal cousin was Yuzhi, courtesy name Zhonglian.

sentences.zh: 少孤，有學業。

translations.literal: In youth he was orphaned; he had learning and accomplishments.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he applied himself to learning.

sentences.zh: 太和中，釋褐奉朝請，廣陵王羽常侍，累歷蕃佐。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, at his first appointment he was Attendant at Court and Regular Attendant to the Prince of Guangling Yu, and successively served as staff in various principalities.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he entered office as Attendant at Court and Regular Attendant to Prince Yu of Guangling, later serving in various princely staffs.

sentences.zh: 入為司空功曹參軍事、太尉主簿，遷冀州撫軍府長史。

translations.literal: He entered service as Merit Evaluation Officer in the Bureau of Works and Chief Clerk of the Defender-in-Chief, then was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Pacification Army headquarters of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He entered central government as Merit Evaluation Officer in the Bureau of Works and Chief Clerk of the Defender-in-Chief, then was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Pacification Army headquarters in Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 後為揚州平東府長史，帶南梁太守。

translations.literal: Later he was Chief Clerk of the Pacifying East Headquarters of Yang Province, concurrently Administrator of Nanliang.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Chief Clerk of the Pacifying East Headquarters in Yang Province, concurrently holding the post of Administrator of Nanliang.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍義州刺史文僧明來降，瑜之迎接有勳，賜爵高邑男。

translations.literal: When Xiao Yan's Inspector of Yi Province Wen Sengming came to surrender, Yuzhi received him with merit and was given the title Baron of Gaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Sengming, Inspector of Yi Province under Xiao Yan, came over in surrender, Yuzhi distinguished himself in receiving him and was enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoyi.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，除鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang he was made Vice Director of the Chamberlain for Dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xiaochang era he was appointed Vice Director of the Chamberlain for Dependencies.

sentences.zh: 三年卒，年五十六。

translations.literal: In the third year he died, at the age of fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiaochang he died at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈平北將軍、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously given General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 有三子。

translations.literal: He had three sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons.

sentences.zh: 長子孟舒，字長才，襲父爵。

translations.literal: His eldest son Mengshu, courtesy name Changcai, inherited his father's title.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Mengshu, courtesy name Changcai, who inherited his father's title.

sentences.zh: 累遷平東將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotion he became General Who Pacifies the East and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotion to General Who Pacifies the East and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 興和中，除廣平太守。

translations.literal: In the Xinghe era he was made Administrator of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xinghe era he was appointed Administrator of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈中軍將軍、殷州刺史，贈平東將軍，[8]諡曰康。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously given General of the Central Army and Inspector of Yin Province, posthumously given General Who Pacifies the East, [8] posthumous name Kang.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously honored as General of the Central Army and Inspector of Yin Province, and again as General Who Pacifies the East; [8] his posthumous name was Kang.

sentences.zh: 孟舒弟仲舒，武定末，鄴縣令。

translations.literal: Mengshu's younger brother Zhongshu, at the end of Wuding, was Magistrate of Ye County.
translations.idiomatic: Mengshu's younger brother Zhongshu served as Magistrate of Ye County at the end of the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 仲舒弟季舒，給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Zhongshu's younger brother Jishu was Attendant Serving Within the Yellow Gates and Gentleman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu's younger brother Jishu served as Attendant Serving Within the Yellow Gates and Gentleman Attendant.

sentences.zh: 挺從祖弟脩和，州主簿。

translations.literal: Ting's younger cousin Xiuhe was Chief Clerk of the province.
translations.idiomatic: Ting's younger cousin Xiuhe served as Chief Clerk of the province.

sentences.zh: 子儉，字元恭，雅有器度。

translations.literal: His son Jian, courtesy name Yuangong, was refined in bearing and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jian, courtesy name Yuangong, was refined in bearing and possessed of capacity.

sentences.zh: 歷太學博士，終於符璽郎中。

translations.literal: He passed through Erudite of the Imperial Academy and ended as Gentleman of the Seals and Credentials.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and ended his career as Gentleman of the Seals and Credentials.

sentences.zh: 儉弟緒，字仲穆。

translations.literal: Jian's younger brother Xu, courtesy name Zhongmu.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's younger brother was Xu, courtesy name Zhongmu.

sentences.zh: 定州撫軍府法曹參軍。

translations.literal: Legal Affairs Officer of the Pacification Army headquarters of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Legal Affairs Officer of the Pacification Army headquarters in Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 緒小弟孝忠，侍御史、祕書郎。

translations.literal: Xu's youngest younger brother Xiaozhong was Attending Censor and Secretary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's youngest brother Xiaozhong served as Attending Censor and Secretary Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 並有容貌，無他才識。

translations.literal: All had fine appearances but no other talent or insight.
translations.idiomatic: All were handsome in appearance but lacked other talent or discernment.

sentences.zh: 緒子子謙，尚書郎。

translations.literal: Xu's son Ziqian was Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's son Ziqian served as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 子謙弟子讓，與侯景同反，子謙坐以囚執，遇病死於晉陽。

translations.literal: Ziqian's younger brother's son Rang rebelled together with Hou Jing; Ziqian was implicated and imprisoned, and died of illness at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ziqian's nephew Rang rebelled together with Hou Jing. Ziqian was implicated, imprisoned, and died of illness at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 子讓弟子廉等，並伏法。

translations.literal: Rang's younger brother's sons Lian and others were all executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Rang's nephews Lian and others were all executed by law.

sentences.zh: 脩和弟敬邕，性長者，有幹用。

translations.literal: Xiuhe's younger brother Jingyong, by nature a man of mature character, had practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuhe's younger brother Jingyong was by nature a man of mature and steady character, possessed of practical ability.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，自司徒主簿轉尚書都官郎中，所在稱職。

translations.literal: During Emperor Gaozu's reign, from Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education he was transferred to Director of Penal Affairs in the Masters of Writing; in every post he was rated as fulfilling his duties.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Gaozu's reign he rose from Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education to Director of Penal Affairs in the Masters of Writing, and in every post was rated as fulfilling his duties.

sentences.zh: 遷太子步兵校尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commandant of Footsoldiers of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commandant of Footsoldiers of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 景明初，母憂去職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming he left office on account of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingming era he left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 後中山王英南討，引為都督府長史，加左中郎將，以功賜爵臨淄男。

translations.literal: Later when the Prince of Zhongshan Ying campaigned south, he was recruited as Chief Clerk of the commander-in-chief's headquarters, with the additional title Left Commandant of the Center, and for merit was given the title Baron of Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Prince Ying of Zhongshan marched south on campaign, Jingyong was recruited as Chief Clerk of the commander-in-chief's headquarters with the additional rank of Left Commandant of the Center, and for his merit was enfeoffed as Baron of Linzi.

sentences.zh: 遷龍驤將軍、太府少卿，以本將軍出除營州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Dragon Cavalry and Vice Director of the Imperial Treasury, and with his former rank went out to be made Inspector of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Dragon Cavalry and Vice Director of the Imperial Treasury, then sent out with his former rank as Inspector of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: [9]庫莫奚國有馬百匹因風入境，敬邕悉令送還，於是夷人感附。

translations.literal: [9] The Kumo Xi state had a hundred horses that entered the border driven by the wind; Jingyong had them all sent back, and thereby the barbarians were moved to attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: [9] A hundred horses from the Kumo Xi entered the border driven by the wind. Jingyong had them all returned, and the barbarian peoples were thereby moved to submit.

sentences.zh: 熙平二年，拜征虜將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiping he was appointed General Who Repels the Barbarians and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiping he was appointed General Who Repels the Barbarians and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 神龜中卒，[10]年五十七。

translations.literal: In the Shengui era he died, [10] at the age of fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Shengui era, [10] at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈左將軍、濟州刺史，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Posthumously given General of the Left and Inspector of Ji Province; posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General of the Left and Inspector of Ji Province; his posthumous name was Gong.

sentences.zh: 子子盛，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Zisheng inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zisheng inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 除奉朝請。

translations.literal: He was made Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 脩和從弟接，字顯賓。

translations.literal: Xiuhe's younger cousin Jie, courtesy name Xianbin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuhe's younger cousin was Jie, courtesy name Xianbin.

sentences.zh: 容貌魁偉，放邁自高，不拘常檢。

translations.literal: His appearance was tall and imposing; he was unrestrained and self-exalted, not bound by conventional restraint.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and imposing in appearance, free-spirited and proud, and unconstrained by conventional propriety.

sentences.zh: 為中書博士、樂陵內史。

translations.literal: He was Erudite of the Central Secretariat and Inner Magistrate of Leling.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Erudite of the Central Secretariat and Inner Magistrate of Leling.

sentences.zh: 雅為任城王澄所禮待，及澄為定州刺史，接了無民敬，王忻然容下之。

translations.literal: He was always treated with courtesy by the Prince of Rencheng Cheng; when Cheng became Inspector of Ding Province, Jie showed no proper deference befitting his office, yet the prince gladly accommodated him.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been treated with courtesy by Prince Cheng of Rencheng. When Cheng became Inspector of Ding Province, Jie showed no proper deference befitting his office, yet the prince graciously tolerated him.

sentences.zh: 後為冀州安東府司馬，轉樂陵太守。

translations.literal: Later he was Chief Administrator of the Pacifying East Headquarters of Ji Province, then transferred to Administrator of Leling.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Chief Administrator of the Pacifying East Headquarters in Ji Province, then was transferred to Administrator of Leling.

sentences.zh: 還鄉而卒。

translations.literal: He returned to his home district and died.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home and died there.

sentences.zh: 挺族子纂，字叔則，博學有文才。

translations.literal: Ting's clansman Zuan, courtesy name Shuze, was broadly learned and had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ting's clansman Zuan, courtesy name Shuze, was broadly learned and possessed literary talent.

sentences.zh: 景明中，太學博士，轉員外散騎侍郎、襄威將軍。

translations.literal: In the Jingming era he was Erudite of the Imperial Academy, then transferred to Extraordinary Attendant of the Loose Cavalry and General Who Displays Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingming era he served as Erudite of the Imperial Academy, then was transferred to Extraordinary Attendant of the Loose Cavalry and General Who Displays Martiality.

sentences.zh: 既不為時知，乃著無談子論。

translations.literal: When he was not recognized by his age, he thereupon composed the Treatise of Master Wutan.
translations.idiomatic: Finding no recognition in his day, he wrote the Treatise of Master Wutan.

sentences.zh: 後為給事中。

translations.literal: Later he was made Gentlemen Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Gentlemen Attendant.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，除梁州征虜府長史。

translations.literal: In the Yanchang era he was appointed Chief Administrator of the Pacifying Barbarians Headquarters of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yanchang era he was appointed Chief Administrator of the Pacifying Barbarians Headquarters in Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 熙平初，為寧遠將軍、廷尉正，每於大獄，多所據明，有當官之譽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiping he was made General Who Pacifies the Distant and Director of the Court of Justice; in major cases he often clarified matters on evidence, winning a reputation for being fit for office.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xiping era he became General Who Pacifies the Distant and Director of the Court of Justice; in major cases he often clarified matters on the evidence, earning a reputation for being fit for his post.

sentences.zh: 時太原王靜自廷尉監遷少卿，纂耻居其下，乃與靜書，辭氣抑揚，無上下之體。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Jing of Taiyuan was transferred from Supervisor of the Court of Justice to Vice Director; Zuan was ashamed to rank below him and so wrote a letter to Jing, with his language rising and falling in tone without the proper respect between superior and subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Jing of Taiyuan was promoted from Supervisor of the Court of Justice to Vice Director. Zuan was ashamed to rank beneath him and wrote Jing a letter whose tone rose and fell without the proper deference owed between superior and subordinate.

sentences.zh: 又啟求解任，乃除左中郎將，領尚書三公郎中。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting relief from his duties, whereupon he was appointed Left Commandant of the Palace Guards and concurrently served as Director of the Three Excellencies Office in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized asking to be relieved of his duties and was then appointed Left Commandant of the Palace Guards, concurrently serving as Director of the Three Excellencies Office in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以公事免。

translations.literal: Before long he was dismissed on account of official business.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was dismissed for an official matter.

sentences.zh: 後為洛陽令。

translations.literal: Later he was made Magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 正光中卒，年四十五。

translations.literal: He died in the Zhengguang era at the age of forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Zhengguang era at the age of forty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒左長史。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded the title of Left Chief Administrator of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded the title of Left Chief Administrator of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 凡所製文，多行於世。

translations.literal: Of all the writings he composed, many circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the writings he composed circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 長子史，武定末，儀同府長流參軍。

translations.literal: His eldest son Shi, at the end of Wuding, was Chief Administrator's Adjutant of Flowing Streams in an Household Equal in Rank to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Shi, at the end of the Wuding era, served as Chief Administrator's Adjutant of Flowing Streams in a household equal in rank to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 纂兄穆，寬雅有度量，州辟主簿。

translations.literal: Zuan's elder brother Mu was broad-minded and refined, possessed of magnanimity; the province recruited him as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's elder brother Mu was broad-minded and refined, possessed of magnanimity; the province recruited him as Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子暹，武定末，度支尚書、兼右僕射。

translations.literal: His son Xian, at the end of Wuding, was Minister of Revenue and concurrently Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xian, at the end of the Wuding era, served as Minister of Revenue and concurrently Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 纂弟融，字脩業。

translations.literal: Zuan's younger brother Rong, courtesy name Xiuye.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's younger brother Rong, courtesy name Xiuye.

sentences.zh: 奉朝請。

translations.literal: Gentlemen Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Gentlemen Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 尚書令高肇出討巴蜀，引為統軍。

translations.literal: When the Director of the Masters of Writing Gao Zhao went out to campaign against Ba and Shu, he recruited him as General-in-Command.
translations.idiomatic: When Director of the Masters of Writing Gao Zhao marched out to campaign against Ba and Shu, he recruited Rong as General-in-Command.

sentences.zh: 還，除員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Upon return he was appointed Extraordinary Attendant of the Loose Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After returning he was appointed Extraordinary Attendant of the Loose Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 正光中，定州別駕。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era he was Vice Administrator of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengguang era he served as Vice Administrator of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 年四十二，卒。

translations.literal: At the age of forty-two he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 子鴻翻，郡功曹。

translations.literal: His son Hongfan was Records Officer of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongfan served as Records Officer of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 纂從祖弟遊，字延叔，少有風概。

translations.literal: Zuan's younger cousin from the paternal line You, courtesy name Yanshu, from youth had bearing and resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's younger paternal cousin You, courtesy name Yanshu, from youth possessed bearing and resolve.

sentences.zh: 釋褐奉朝請，稍遷太尉主簿。

translations.literal: On first donning the un dyed robe he was Gentlemen Attendant at Court, and was gradually promoted to Chief Clerk of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On first entering office he was Gentlemen Attendant at Court and was gradually promoted to Chief Clerk of the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史陳伯之啟為司馬，還除奉車都尉。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Jiang Province Chen Buzhi requested him as Chief Administrator; upon return he was appointed Commandant Who Carries Imperial Vehicles.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Jiang Province Chen Buzhi requested him as Chief Administrator; after returning he was appointed Commandant Who Carries Imperial Vehicles.

sentences.zh: 大都督、中山王英征義陽，引為錄事參軍，尋轉司馬。

translations.literal: The Grand Commander, Prince of Zhongshan Ying, on campaign against Yiyang recruited him as Recording Adjutant, and soon after he was transferred to Chief Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commander, Prince of Zhongshan Ying, on campaign against Yiyang recruited him as Recording Adjutant; he was soon transferred to Chief Administrator.

sentences.zh: 及英敗於鍾離，遊坐徙秦州，久而得還。

translations.literal: When Ying was defeated at Zhongli, You was implicated and exiled to Qin Province; after a long time he was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying was defeated at Zhongli, You was implicated and exiled to Qin Province; only after a long interval was he able to return.

sentences.zh: 大將軍高肇西征，引為統軍，除步兵校尉，遷豫州征虜府長史，未幾，除征虜將軍、北趙郡太守，並有政績。

translations.literal: The Great General Gao Zhao on his western campaign recruited him as General-in-Command; he was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers, then transferred to Chief Administrator of the Pacifying Barbarians Headquarters of Yu Province; before long he was appointed General Who Pacifies Barbarians and Administrator of North Zhao Commandery — in all these posts he had administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: On Great General Gao Zhao's western campaign he recruited You as General-in-Command. You was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers, then transferred to Chief Administrator of the Pacifying Barbarians Headquarters in Yu Province; before long he was made General Who Pacifies Barbarians and Administrator of North Zhao Commandery, and in every post achieved notable administrative success.

sentences.zh: 熙平末，轉河東太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiping he was transferred to Administrator of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xiping era he was transferred to Administrator of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 郡有鹽戶，常供州郡為兵，子孫見丁從役，遊矜其勞苦，乃表聞請聽更代，郡內感之。

translations.literal: The commandery had salt households who regularly supplied men for military service to the province and commandery; descendants were liable for conscription as they came of age. You took pity on their toil and hardship and so submitted a memorial requesting that rotation of service be permitted; the people within the commandery were moved by this.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery had salt households who regularly supplied conscripts to the province and commandery; descendants were liable for service as they came of age. You took pity on their hardship and submitted a memorial asking that rotation of duty be permitted, and the people of the commandery were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 太學舊在城內，遊乃移置城南閑敞之處，親自說經，當時學者莫不勸慕，號為良守。

translations.literal: The Imperial Academy had formerly been inside the city walls; You moved it to an open, spacious place south of the city and personally lectured on the classics. Scholars of the time all admired and aspired to this, and he was called a good Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Academy had formerly stood inside the city walls; You moved it to an open, spacious site south of the city and personally lectured on the classics. Scholars of the day all admired and aspired to study there, and he was hailed as a good Administrator.

sentences.zh: 以本將軍遷涼州刺史，以母憂解任。

translations.literal: With his existing rank of general he was transferred to Inspector of Liang Province, but left office on account of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Retaining his general's rank, he was transferred to Inspector of Liang Province but left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 正光中，起除右將軍、南秦州刺史，固辭不免。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era he was summoned and appointed Right General and Inspector of South Qin Province; he firmly declined but could not avoid appointment.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengguang era he was summoned and appointed Right General and Inspector of South Qin Province; he firmly declined but could not escape appointment.

sentences.zh: 先是，州人楊松柏、楊洛德兄弟數為反叛，遊至州，深加招慰。

translations.literal: Previously, the natives of the province, the brothers Yang Songbai and Yang Luode, had repeatedly rebelled. When You arrived at the province he greatly extended outreach and consolation.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the brothers Yang Songbai and Yang Luode, natives of the province, had repeatedly rebelled. When You arrived he extended generous outreach and consolation.

sentences.zh: 松柏歸款，引為主簿，稍以辭色誘之，兄弟俱至。

translations.literal: Songbai submitted in good faith; You appointed him Chief Clerk and gradually lured him with friendly words and manner until both brothers came.
translations.idiomatic: Songbai submitted in good faith; You appointed him Chief Clerk and gradually drew him in with friendly words and manner until both brothers came.

sentences.zh: 松柏既州之豪帥，感遊恩遇，奬諭羣氐，咸來歸款，且以過在前政，不復自疑。

translations.literal: Since Songbai was a powerful leader of the province, moved by You's kindness he encouraged and instructed the various Di peoples, who all came to submit in good faith; moreover, because the fault lay with the previous administration, they no longer doubted themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Songbai was a powerful leader of the province; moved by You's kindness, he encouraged the various Di peoples, who all came to submit in good faith. Because the fault had lain with the previous administration, they no longer held themselves in doubt.

sentences.zh: 遊乃因宴會，一時俱斬，於是外人以其不信，合境皆反。

translations.literal: You then seized the occasion of a banquet and executed them all at once. Thereupon outsiders, judging him untrustworthy, rebelled throughout the entire territory.
translations.idiomatic: You then used a banquet as his occasion and executed them all at once. Outsiders, judging him untrustworthy, rebelled throughout the entire province.

sentences.zh: 正光五年夏，秦州城人殺刺史李彥據州為逆。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifth year of Zhengguang, the people of Qin Province's capital city killed the Inspector Li Yan and seized the province in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fifth year of Zhengguang, the people of Qin Province's capital killed Inspector Li Yan and seized the province in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 數日之後，遊知必不安，謀欲出外，尋為城人韓祖香、孫𥛰攻於州館。

translations.literal: Several days later You knew he could not remain secure and planned to go outside; soon afterward he was attacked at the provincial hostel by the city men Han Zuxiang and Sun Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later You knew he could not remain secure and planned to leave; soon he was attacked at the provincial hostel by the city men Han Zuxiang and Sun Yan.

sentences.zh: 遊事窘，登樓慷慨悲歎，乃推下小女而殺之，義不為羣小所辱也。

translations.literal: You, pressed hard, mounted a tower and lamented with passionate grief; he then pushed down his young daughter and killed her, refusing on principle to let the rabble dishonor him.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, You mounted a tower and lamented with passionate grief; he then pushed his young daughter down and killed her, refusing on principle to let the mob dishonor him.

sentences.zh: 尋為祖香等所執害，時年五十二。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was seized and killed by Zuxiang and the others; he was fifty-two years old.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was seized and killed by Zuxiang and the others; he was fifty-two years old.

sentences.zh: 永安中，贈散騎侍郎、鎮北將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era he was posthumously awarded Attendant of the Loose Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yong'an era he was posthumously awarded Attendant of the Loose Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 子伏護，開府參軍。

translations.literal: His son Fuhu was Staff Officer of the General-in-Chief's Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fuhu served as Staff Officer of the General-in-Chief's Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：高祐學業優通，知名前世，儒俊之風，門舊不隕。

translations.literal: The historian says: Gao You's learning and accomplishments were excellent and comprehensive; renowned in earlier generations, the scholarly excellence of his house did not fade.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Gao You's learning and accomplishments were excellent and comprehensive; renowned in earlier generations, the scholarly brilliance of his house did not fade.

sentences.zh: 諸子經傳之器，加有捨生之節。

translations.literal: His sons were vessels of the classics and commentaries, and moreover possessed the integrity to give up their lives.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were fit vessels of the classics and commentaries, and moreover possessed the integrity to give up their lives.

sentences.zh: 崔挺兄弟，風操高亮，懷文抱質，歷事著稱，見重於朝野，繼世承家，門族並著，蓋所謂彼有人焉。

translations.literal: The brothers Cui Ting bore lofty conduct and bright integrity, treasured literature and embraced substance; in successive service they won notable acclaim and were esteemed in court and countryside alike. Carrying on the family line from generation to generation, the whole clan was eminent — this is what is meant by "over there they have their men."
translations.idiomatic: The brothers Cui Ting bore lofty conduct and bright integrity, treasured literature and embraced substance; in successive service they won notable acclaim and were esteemed in court and countryside alike. Carrying on the family from generation to generation, the whole clan was eminent — this is what is meant by "over there they have their men."

translations.literal: In narrating Gao You's words, the complete Wei shu agrees with the Baiken edition; knowing that the old Wei shu text seen by Sima Guang was just so, editions from the Southern edition downward must have been altered and supplemented according to Beishi.
translations.idiomatic: In narrating Gao You's words, the complete Wei shu agrees with the Baiken edition; since the old Wei shu text Sima Guang saw read just so, editions from the Southern edition downward must have been altered and supplemented from Beishi.

sentences.zh: 且上文只說「縣黨宜有黌序」，沒有提到村，北魏鄉閭組織也沒有村的一級。

translations.literal: Moreover, the text above speaks only of "counties and communities ought to have schools"; it does not mention villages, and the neighborhood organization of Northern Wei also had no village tier.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the passage above speaks only of "counties and communities ought to have schools"; it does not mention villages, and Northern Wei's neighborhood organization likewise had no village tier.

sentences.zh: 雖北史或有所本，却未必是魏書脫誤，今從百衲本。

translations.literal: Although Beishi may have had some source, it need not be a lacuna or error in Wei shu; now follow the Baiken edition.
translations.idiomatic: Although Beishi may have had some source, that need not mean Wei shu is lacunose or corrupt; the text now follows the Baiken edition.

translations.idiomatic: Prose without rhyme was then called bi (brush); Beishi is probably correct.

translations.literal: Soon made Extraordinary Attendant of the Loose Cavalry and General Who Displays Authority — According to juan 113 Offices and Clans Treatise post-Taihe rank table, General Who Displays Authority is sixth rank; here below "jiang" (general) the character "jun" (army/military) is omitted.
translations.idiomatic: "Soon made Extraordinary Attendant of the Loose Cavalry and General Who Displays Authority": per juan 113, Offices and Clans Treatise, post-Taihe rank table, General Who Displays Authority is sixth rank; here jun (army) is omitted after jiang (general).

sentences.zh: 贈中軍將軍殷州刺史贈平東將軍 北史卷三二崔挺傳附見孟舒作「贈殷州刺史、鎮東將軍」。
